articles.title_orig: Israel Election Live Updates: Record Voter Turnout as Netanyahu Faces Challenge Led by Eisenkot
articles.title_zh: Israel Election Live Updates: Record Voter Turnout as Netanyahu Faces Challenge Led by Eisenkot
articles.content_orig:
By early afternoon almost 45% of voters had cast their ballot
What you need to know about Israel’s election
We’ve reported on how many Israelis are viewing this election as one of the most important of their lifetime, and politicians across the spectrum have characterised it as “existential” for the future of the Israeli state.
That urgency does appear to be translating into record turn-out at the polls according to latest figures from the Central Elections Committee.
As of 2pm local time, 44.9% of voters had cast their ballot . This is the highest turn-out since record keeping began in the 1970s. The voting level at this hour is also about 6% higher than the last election in 2022, where Netanyahu was ultimately able to scrape together a slim majority coalition with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties.
The queues are so long today that the electoral authority has also issued fresh guidance on how to ease congestion; advising polling staff to start verifying voters’ IDs while they’re still in line. Voting is open until 10pm local time and any eligible Israeli who arrives by a polling station by then can cast their vote. As we’ve reported, many eligible voters have also flown back into the country for the sole purpose of making their ballot count today.
The Palestinian Israeli vote is a critical camp in this election, representing about one fifth of all eligible voters. Their votes are expected to go to either Ra’am, led by Mansour Abbas, or Joint List, an electoral alliance of Palestinian-Israeli parties. But for them them, change will not be straightforward, as my colleague Julian Borger in Nazareth writes. Even if the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot wins more seats than Netanyahu’s coalition, it is not expected to win an outright majority on its own, and it has so far ruled out going into coalition with the Palestinian Israeli parties, who could well hold the balance of power ones the votes are counted. Amjad Shbita, the general secretary of Hadash, the leading party in the Joint List coalition, thought that the Eisenkot’s approach might change after the elections. “He cannot sit down [in coalition] with Netanyahu, and he won’t want to go back to another round of elections, so we think he can be flexible,” he said.
In Nazareth, the largest Palestinian-majority town in Israel , the turnout at polling stations has been noticeably stronger than last elections. By 2pm the turnout was over 32%, up from 28% at this time four years ago. That was still below the average Jewish turnout across the country, but a surge of evening voting is expected here as voters come home from work. At the headquarters of the Joint List, the biggest coalition of Palestinian-Israeli parties, the most pressing concern was the spoiler tactics of far-right election monitors at the predominantly Palestinian polling stations. “They can say that they want to check all the voter numbers and identity and everything, so they can slow things down, so that people wait a long time and give up. That’s their intention,” Amjad Shbita, the general secretary of Hadash, a socialist movement which is the leading party in the Joint List coalition. At the worst, these tactical ploys have slowed the process down so that it took 30 minutes to vote, rather than just a couple, he said. The Joint List sent its workers out to the polling station to provide water and folding chairs so that voters would not lose patience and go home. Shbita said that Palestinian Israel motivation is strong enough to overcome such obstacles. “It is the first time for a long time that a government has stayed in office for its full term, four years,” he said. “We are talking about one of the worst governments when it comes to Arab society. We feel racism at all levels of Israeli society, in hospitals, in buses, in public transportation, in the media. So people understand that today we have the opportunity to change the government.”
Voter turn-out is shattering all records. 55.7% of eligible Israelis had cast their votes by 4pm local time , according to the latest numbers from the Central Elections Committee.
That’s an 8.2% increase from the 2022 vote.
Polls are open until 10pm local time, after which the first exit polls will come out.
Voters have turned out in droves at polling stations across the country.
Amid the highest voter turnout in decades, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies resorted to racist scare tactics , including unsubstantiated allegations of election fraud, to urge their own voters to the polls.
“We’re in a war for our home,” Netanyahu said in a social media post in the early afternoon, with unsourced claims of low voter turnouts in strongholds of his Likud party. “Muslim Brotherhood supporters are raiding the polling stations and stealing the elections. Go out and vote, recover it!”
In 2015, Netanyahu claimed that “Arab voters are coming out in droves to the polls” in a bid to motivate his party’s base. The comments drew a rebuke from then-US President Barack Obama and Netanyahu apologised for them soon after winning another mandate.
A decade later he is doubling down on that political tactic. A robo-call to voters purporting to come from the prime minister made groundless accusations that Palestinian citizens of Israel were trying to “steal the election”. A spokesman for Netanyahu did not respond to questions about the call.
In the call, a man who sounds like the prime minister falsely claims that three leaders of the Ra’am party had been caught with envelopes full of cash. He also says that left wing women were driving Palestinian women to polling stations, which is not illegal under Israeli law.
He finishes by urging his own voters to turn out. Polling day is a holiday for most Israelis, who often use it to go to the beach, hiking or other activities with their family.
“You need to go to the polling stations. Everyone needs to vote. There is no beach. No barbecue, there is nothing (else) now,” it says. “Everyone must go out to vote to ensure the victory of the right against the left.”
Earlier he shared photos that purported to show empty polling stations in Likud-supporting areas, and long lines in opposition strongholds. The Guardian saw long queues on Tuesday morning in areas with high support for Netanyahu and his allies, including parts of Jerusalem and the settlement of Efrat.
After casting his own ballot, far right Jewish supremacist Itamar Ben Gvir went to a Palestinian- majority town to make similar claims. “Now in Kfar Qasim. Don’t let them win”, he posted above a social media video filmed on the outskirts of the town, the site of a notorious massacre by Israeli border police in 1956.
“Voter turnout in the Arab sector is off the charts, unprecedented.” he says. “If you want this country to remain Jewish and Zionist...then get out and vote.”
The US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has just issued a clarification on his election day tweet this morning which prompted a few raised eyebrows. Earlier he’d written on X:
double quotation mark Today is election day in Israel, which is a national holiday. All voting is in person, ID required. No mail-in or absentee ballots. Arabs vote same as Israelis. Contentious process, but it’s a democracy-not many of those in this region!
The “Arabs vote same as Israelis” phrasing was perceived by some as appearing to imply that Arab voters in Israel aren’t Israeli or due the same vote.
Huckabee’s since posted a follow-up, agreeing with Axios journalist Barak Ravid who pointed out “Mr Ambassador, the Arabs who vote are Israelis…”. "Correct and I should have stated it that way!” said Huckabee.
double quotation mark 10 million ppl in 8m Jews, 2m Arabs. ALL are Israeli citizens-Jew, Muslim, or Christian. All vote, serve in IDF, in Knesset, & proudly have Israeli passports. Women equal to men. All have free speech.

articles.title_orig: Finland and Norway Hold ‘Frank’ Call With Putin on Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Finland and Norway Hold ‘Frank’ Call With Putin on Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Norway and Finland say they are not acting on behalf of other European leaders
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - a rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
The aim was looking at "future negotiations to help to end the war" in Ukraine, the offices of President Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re said. Their initiative was not on behalf of "Europe as a whole".
After the call, Putin said "confrontational" EU and Nato policies were prolonging the war which began when Russia launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has spoken to the two Nordic leaders after their conversation with Putin. Last week, Zelensky met them as well as US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo.
The Ukrainian leader said he was grateful for the "active support" of his Finnish and Norwegian counterparts.
Tuesday's 90-minute phone call was held from the Finnish capital Helsinki, and showed "big differences in views", StÃ¸re said.
Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the call to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.
The call was "frank and substantive", Stubb said, explaining that the war's outcome will "have a direct impact on our and the broader European security".
StÃ¸re added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."
The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.
He - like Stubb and StÃ¸re - had agreed to continue their direct phone communication, the statement added.
Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push
StÃ¸re said all their allies had been informed of the call ahead of time.
Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was "very sceptical" of Tuesday's dialogue, telling Danish broadcaster DR, it had not been "co-ordinated with any of the rest of us".
Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates, was "moderately optimistic".
Relations between the US, Ukraine and its European allies have been souring since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia - allowing it to export oil to the US.
But last week, Stubb, StÃ¸re and Zelesnky met Witkoff in the Norwegian capital, before the US special envoy travelled on to St Petersburg to meet Putin.
Following the talks, Ukraine, Russia and the US agreed to resume three-way negotiations that Russia had stopped for months.
After speaking to the two Nordic leaders, Zelensky said part of their discussions with Putin had centred on November's trilateral talks to be held in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky said he had discussed with them "various formats for our engagement with partners in Europe that could be useful in further supporting diplomacy, our defense, and our shared security".
Stubb and StÃ¸re are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.
As the US administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.
Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the European Union of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.
But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".

articles.title_orig: Argentina Denies Flávio Bolsonaro Entered the Country
articles.title_zh: Argentina Denies Flávio Bolsonaro Entered the Country
articles.content_orig:
Far-right senator banned from leaving country as supreme court judge’s ruling cites money-laundering case
The far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro was banned from leaving Brazil and ordered to surrender his passports just hours after his dramatic loss in the presidential election to the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva .
The ruling was issued by Alexandre de Moraes, the same supreme court justice who oversaw the trial of the senator’s father, the former president Jair Bolsonaro, for attempting a coup.
Bolsonaro posted a video saying the decision was based on an interview his brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro, gave last Friday urging his brother to leave Brazil if he lost the election.
On Monday night, Bolsonaro’s party issued a statement acknowledging the election result, saying: “We recognise the presidential result proclaimed by the electoral court, but believe that the questions raised need to be properly clarified through a balanced and democratic political debate.”
Bolsonaro, like his father four years ago, has still not conceded defeat to Lula.
The court’s brief ruling regarding his passport only refers to a criminal case in which the federal police are investigating Flávio Bolsonaro over his possible involvement in a money-laundering scheme . The ruling orders him not to have any contact with his friend Willer Tomaz, a lawyer linked to betting companies that police suspect were being used to launder about £680m.
It also cancelled all of Bolsonaro’s passports, including the diplomatic one he holds as a congressman, and ordered him to hand them over within 24 hours.
Bolsonaro was the first to speak publicly about the matter, before Brazilian media were even aware of the judge’s decision.
In a video posted on social media, he said he had just left a visit to his father, who is under house arrest in Brasília, when “Lula’s federal police were at his door and in the middle of the street, and I was served with an order to hand over my passports and I am also prohibited from leaving the country”.
He added that, although his brother – who is in self-imposed exile in the US – told a US podcast on Friday that he favoured the senator leaving Brazil if he lost the election, “I never said that”.
When his Senate term ends early next year, Bolsonaro will be out of public office for the first time in 24 years, and therefore without the special immunity afforded to officeholders.
He is under investigation in another criminal case, too, over what happened to the £20m he was captured on tape asking a disgraced banker accused of corruption to provide for a biopic about his father.
The Folha de S Paulo newspaper reported that Flávio Bolsonaro had been persuaded to drop his plan to seek to annul the election, which he had announced after the result was declared on Sunday night.
Bolsonaro had claimed that the two-hour extension of voting – intended to allow voters who had been unable to access the mandatory free public transport to cast their ballots – had harmed the election, despite the fact that his own campaign had also argued for an extension.
According to the newspaper, allies and lawyers told him his argument was legally weak.
Bolsonaro had still not publicly reversed his demand for an annulment, and in the same video he said he would file another case to have Lula’s ticket disqualified over alleged abuse of economic power, a similar case to others his legal team brought during the campaign.

articles.title_orig: US Consumer Confidence Rises for First Time in Four Months
articles.title_zh: US Consumer Confidence Rises for First Time in Four Months
articles.content_orig:
Kitco NEWS has a diverse team of journalists reporting on the economy, stock markets, commodities, cryptocurrencies, mining and metals with accuracy and objectivity. Our goal is to help people make informed market decisions through in-depth reporting, daily market roundups, interviews with prominent industry figures, comprehensive coverage (often exclusive) of important industry events and analyses of market-affecting developments.
(Kitco News) - Gold prices are trading at session highs after the latest data showed an improving picture of the attitudes of U.S. consumers this month.
The Consumer Confidence Index rose to 91.7 in October, above economists’ consensus forecast for an 81 reading and also above the upwardly revised 84.2 print from September, the Conference Board announced on Tuesday.
The Present Situation Index—based on consumers' assessment of current business and labor market conditions—increased by 8.6 points to 120.4. The Expectations Index—based on consumers' short-term outlook for income, business, and labor market conditions—recovered by 6.9 points to 72.6, only partially reversing three consecutive monthly declines. The survey period for this month's preliminary results was October 1 - 21.
Gold prices were setting fresh session highs in the wake of the 10 am ET data release, with spot gold last trading at $4,048.48 per ounce at the time of writing for a gain of 0.78% on the daily chart.
“Consumer confidence advanced in October, driven primarily by improved perceptions of current and expected business conditions,” said Fergus McCormick, Senior Economist, Global Indicators at The Conference Board. “The recovery was in line with retail gasoline prices easing from September to October. Yet, despite the increase in October, consumer confidence remained on the long-term downward trend that's persisted over the past few years. Consumers planned less spending on services and durable goods over the next six months. This likely reflected higher price levels and persistent inflation, which eroded consumers' purchasing power.”
“Among write-in responses in October, consumers continued to express frustration with rising costs,” he added. “References to prices, the high cost of food and groceries, and oil and diesel prices rose. Comments about war and conflict eased for a second straight month but remained elevated. Mentions of jobs and employment as an area of concern also ticked up, though to a lesser extent.”
“On a six-month moving average basis, only consumers under age 35 and those with a household income of $100k or more expressed an increase in confidence,” the report noted. “By generation, confidence amongst Gen X, Baby Boomers, and the Silent Generation continued to trail significantly behind Gen Z and Millennials, widening a sharp generational divide that has emerged over the past two years. In October, confidence improved across all political affiliations—but much more so for Republicans.”
Consumers' average 12-month inflation expectations declined in October but remained elevated at 5.8%,” the Conference Board said. “Consumers still expected higher interest rates over the next 12 months. Overall, more consumers in October expected stock prices to increase rather than decrease in the next 12 months.”
Jeffrey Roach, Chief Economist at LPL Financial, noted that business conditions and discretionary spending both improved in October.
"Business conditions are the best since April when consensus believed the war with Iran would be short-lived, inflation was less sticky, and the AI-trade dominated headlines," he said. "Even more noteworthy, the top five spending plans included restaurants and movies. Several discretionary sectors are vibrant, although consumers said they will cut back on hotels and airfare."
Roach pointed out that employment opportunities also appeared more plentiful, and home buying plans improved for the third consecutive month.
"Consumers may be tightening their belts, but some experiences are still a priority," he said. "Given the other data on core capital shipments, auto sales, and broader consumer spending, Q3 economic growth will likely be above 3% as the economy plows ahead, elevating annual growth to 2.2% for the full year."
Ernest Hoffman is a Crypto and Market Reporter for Kitco News. He has over 15 years of experience as a writer, editor, broadcaster and producer for media, educational and cultural organizations. Ernest began working in market news in 2007, establishing the broadcast division of CEP News in Montreal, Canada, where he developed the fastest web-based audio news service in the world and produced economic news videos in partnership with MSN and the TMX. He has a Bachelor's degree Specialization in Journalism from Concordia University. You can reach Ernest at 1-514-670-1339.

articles.title_orig: S&P 500, Nasdaq advance as oil eases ahead of Fed decision
articles.title_zh: S&P 500, Nasdaq advance as oil eases ahead of Fed decision
articles.content_orig:
NEW YORK (AP) — Wall Street is ticking higher Tuesday as stocks in the artificial-intelligence industry support the market, at least for now.
The S&P 500 rose 0.5% and pulled within 1.3% of its all-time high set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 27 points, or 0.1%, as of 11 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 0.9% higher.
The majority of stocks within the S&P 500 were falling, but gains for several influential AI stocks made up for that. Such stocks have been swerving for weeks on worries about whether their boom is under threat because of how expensive it’s become for companies to borrow money to build data centers and buy more AI chips.
Broadcom climbed 3.3% after announcing a $63 billion financing deal where several Wall Street firms will help Anthropic get access to Broadcom’s XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions.
Elsewhere in the industry, Advanced Micro Devices rose 4% and was one of the strongest forces pushing up on the S&P 500 after Broadcom. CoreWeave, a company that’s borrowed money to buy AI chips that it rents out to customers over the cloud, rose 5.2%, though it’s been careening between big gains and losses within each of the past few days.
General Motors climbed 6.3% after saying it’s moving its stock from a listing on the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq. The automaker said the Nasdaq, which is home to several of the world’s biggest technology stocks, is a fit for its tech-driven strategy. The move could also allow GM to join the Nasdaq 100 index, which would force investment funds that mimic the index to buy it.
GM began trading on the NYSE in 1911.
JetBlue Airways flew 20% higher even though it reported a larger loss for the summer than analysts expected. CEO Joanna Geraghty said the company expects to return to making sustained operating profits next year and to deliver at least $1 in earnings per share in 2028.
Investors may have been bracing for something worse after the airline’s stock came into the day with a loss of nearly 48% for the year so far.
Another travel company, Royal Caribbean Group, also helped lead the market and rose 7.5%. The cruise operator delivered a stronger profit for the summer than analysts expected, while raising its forecast for profit over the full year.
Companies overall are under pressure to deliver big growth in profits. Expectations are high among financial analysts and investors, and that’s what allowed their stock prices to run to records recently despite high inflation, high interest rates and other concerns weighing on the market.
Boeing fell 9.4% after reporting a larger loss for the latest quarter than analysts expected.
Hilton Worldwide Holdings sank 2.8% after reporting weaker revenue for the summer than analysts expected. It also gave a range as a forecast for profit in the final three months of the year whose midpoint fell below analysts’ expectations. The hotel company said it expects to see “increased impact from the Middle East” during the quarter.
Sherwin-Williams fell 1.6% after delivering a weaker profit than analysts expected. High mortgage rates have helped chill the housing industry, which in turn pressures demand for the paints and coatings Sherwin-Williams sells.
“Customer sentiment and the leading indicators we track point to muted demand over the remainder of the year and into 2027,” CEO Heidi Petz said. At the same time, her company is dealing with inflation pushing up its costs for raw materials.
Confidence among U.S. shoppers has tumbled recently as pressure keeps building on them from high inflation. But a report on Tuesday said that U.S. consumer confidence improved in October, when economists expected further weakening.
In the bond market, Treasury yields held relatively steady a day before the Federal Reserve is scheduled to announce its latest decision on interest rates. The Fed last month hiked the fed funds rate for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing inflation, but the widespread expectation on Wall Street is that it will hold rates steady this time.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury eased to 4.98% from 5.00% late Monday.
Helping to keep yields in check was a drop for oil prices. The price for a barrel of Brent crude fell 1.2% to $109.43.
In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed across Europe and Asia. Stocks jumped 3.1% in Seoul and fell 1.3% in Shanghai for two of the bigger moves.
AP Writers Elaine Lai and Matt Ott contributed to this report.

articles.title_zh: Apple unveils new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip
articles.content_orig:

Apple on Tuesday unveiled its new 14-inch MacBook Pro, powered by its latest M6 chip. The new MacBook Pro has 24 hours of battery life and now supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity. The laptop starts at $1,999 and is available in space black and silver.
Apple also announced its latest iMac , which is also powered by the M6 chip. The tech giant revealed the new devices just a day before its “Pro and Tell” event scheduled for Wednesday. On Monday, Apple announced its new iPad mini .
The tech giant says the M6 chip features a 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core and a 12-core GPU that delivers more responsive performance, up to 30% faster graphics, and up to 25% faster AI workloads compared with the M5 chip.
The M6 delivers up to 13 times the LLM prompt-processing speed of the M1 MacBook Pro and up to 1.3 times faster performance than the M5 model, Apple says.
The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, and has memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s, up from the 153GB/s on the M5 chip.
It includes HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack. Like previous models, the laptop features a 12-megapixel camera.
The M6 MacBook Pro supports fast charging, reaching up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with a compatible high-wattage USB-C power adapter.
As for the new M6-powered iMac, it features a faster CPU and GPU, with Neural Accelerators built into every core. Apple says the M6 delivers smooth multitasking and powerful performance for everyday apps, photo editing, and video production.
The new iMac starts at $1,499 and comes in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver.
The company also notes that the new iMac delivers up to five times faster on-device AI performance than the M4 model. It features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, an advanced camera and audio system, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports, color-matched accessories, and macOS 27.
Both the new MacBook Pro and iMac can be preordered starting October 28 and will be available starting November 6.

articles.title_orig: Everything Apple Announced This Week So Far: New iPad And MacBooks
articles.title_zh: Everything Apple Announced This Week So Far: New iPad And MacBooks
articles.content_orig:
Ahead of its 'Pro and Tell' event, the company has already launched a few new devices.
Apple wasn't done with its product reveals for the fall after unveiling the iPhone Duo , iPhone 18 Pro models and an array of smart home devices . Nor could it wait until the third event of the season, dubbed Pro and Tell, to show off more gear.
The company got a string of announcements underway on Monday with the reveal of the long-awaited OLED iPad mini. Tuesday brought us an M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro. It's expected that Apple will unveil a touchscreen MacBook as well.
Elsewhere, Apple released the latest versions of its operating systems. Among other things, those added more Siri AI features and made the assistant available in more languages. The company updated Apple Creator Studio with more AI features and creative tools as well.
We'll update this story if and when Apple makes more announcements. In the meantime, here's everything Apple has announced so far this week.
It feels like we've been waiting for forever for Apple to put an OLED display in the iPad mini but that day has finally arrived. The new display has double the peak brightness of the one on the previous model at 1,200 nits, and it has a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The base storage remains the same at 128GB, though if you opt for 256GB or 512GB of storage, you can snag a variant with a nano-texture glass display. That'll cost you extra, naturally.
The company managed to squeeze in a larger screen — an 8.5-inch display rather than the 8.3-inch one in the previous model — without increasing the size of the tablet. In fact, the new iPad mini is slightly narrower than the last one, at 5.22 inches vs. 5.3 inches. It's lighter as well, with the Wi-Fi model coming in at 0.56 pounds (compared with 0.65 pounds last time) and the 5G variant weighing 0.58 pounds (versus 0.66 pounds). The latter, by the way, now boasts Apple's C2 modem, which is said to deliver up to 50 percent faster data speeds than the previous iPad mini. There's also Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity thanks to the N1 chip.
The OLED iPad mini — the eighth generation of the device — runs on the A20 Pro, the same chipset as the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Apple says the SoC is capable of running large language models locally, in case you're into that kind of thing. Otherwise, the tablet should be notably faster than earlier models. It supports Apple Intelligence and Siri AI as well, of course. The chipset also boasts a 7-core GPU — two more cores than the A17 Pro, which powered the last-gen iPad mini.
On the camera front, there's a 12MP Center Stage lens on front of the tablet, which Apple has finally shifted to the landscape edge on the iPad mini. However, there's still no Face ID. The 12MP camera on the rear supports 4K 60fps video capture and Smart HDR 4.
The 8th-gen iPad mini has a sealed enclosure to help protect it from the elements. The tablet has an IP67 rating, meaning that it should withstand dust and being immersed in a meter of freshwater for up to 30 minutes, though I would advise against intentionally submerging your iPad mini.
As for battery life, Apple says that should be roughly the same as last time. The company says the new iPad mini should run for up to 10 hours when you're watching video or surfing the web over Wi-Fi. That drops down to nine hours if you're browsing over a cellular connection. If you have at least a 35W power adaptor, you'll be able to recharge the battery to 50 percent of its capacity in 30 minutes, Apple says.
The most interesting thing to me about this iPad mini is that it has Apple's first Acoustic Display, which the company says helps it deliver "an even better audio experience." It claims the tablet offers more volume and "punchier bass" thanks to woofers that "are paired through the display." Apple added that "custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs." I'm definitely curious to find out how all of that sounds in practice.
Inevitably, the latest iPad mini comes with a price hike. It starts at $699, which is $150 more than the previous model after Apple increased the price of that in June . Pre-orders open on October 28, and the tablet will hit shelves on November 6.
On Tuesday, Apple gave the iMac and MacBook Pro spec bumps. The desktop and laptop now each have the M6 chipset , which recently debuted in the Mac mini .
Let's start with the new iMac . Apple says the M6's dual 16-core neural engine enables it to deliver up to five times faster on-device AI performance (for Siri AI, Apple Intelligence and local LLMs) than the previous-gen iMac from 2024 , which had the M4 chipset. The M6 is said to deliver up to 1.5 times faster performance than the M4 for daily tasks, up to two times faster graphics performance (for photo editing etc.) and up to two times higher gaming performance with ray tracing.
The base-level M6 has 10 CPU cores (two super, three performance and two efficiency cores) and a 10-core CPU, compared with eight of each in the M4. There's the option to have a 12-core M6, in which case your desktop will have four Thunderbolt 4 ports instead of the two that the base model has. The four-port model has a nano-texture glass option as well.
Elsewhere, Apple has introduced its N1 networking chip to the iMac. As such, the computer has support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity. It also has the option to add a 2.5Gb Ethernet port, an upgrade from gigabit Ethernet on the M4 iMac.
Specs otherwise are the same as last time. You'll still get a 24-inch 4.5K Super Retina display, a 12MP Center Stage camera, a six‑speaker Dolby Atmos system, at least 16GB of RAM and 256GB of base storage. The dimensions are identical too, though the M6 iMac is a touch lighter than the previous gen at 9.7 pounds (versus 9.74 pounds). Don't expect any changes to the color options either — the new iMac is still available in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver.
One other thing that's staying the same? The starting price, at least after the $200 increase that Apple gave the M4 iMac over the summer. The new model starts at $1,499, and the four-port version will run you at least $1,699. Pre-orders open October 28 and you'll be able to pick one up in store on November 6.
The latest 14-inch MacBook Pro has the 12-core version of the M6 chipset and the N1 networking chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. Those appear to be the only spec changes this time.
Compared with the previous-gen 14-inch MBP, which had an M5 SoC, Apple says the M6 model offers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads. It's said to deliver up to 1.3 faster rendering performance with ray tracing in Blender, up to 1.2 times faster image-processing performance in Affinity and up to 1.3 faster project build performance for compiling code in Xcode.
It doesn't seem like this will be a massive upgrade for folks with an M5 model. However, if you have an older MacBook Pro (or really need those incremental improvements from the previous gen), it might be worth making the switch.
At least you won't have to pay more than you would have for the M5 model following this summer's price increase . The M6-powered 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 for 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. Again, pre-orders start on Wednesday with general availability to follow on November 6.

The State Department has ordered non-emergency government personnel and their families to evacuate Saudi Arabia following a surge in missile and drone strikes targeting civilian airports and critical infrastructure across the kingdom.
In a security alert issued Tuesday, the U.S. warned that ongoing hostilities by Iran-backed Houthi forces have caused severe travel disruptions and civilian casualties, prompting strict travel restrictions for American personnel and warnings of wider regional spillover.
"Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," according to the alert.
"The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area."
Flight operations remain severely disrupted across major transit hubs, including Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport , where only limited routes are running, alongside significant delays at facilities in Jeddah and Dammam.
U.S. officials urged private citizens to exercise extreme caution, consider overland transit alternatives via operational borders like the King Fahd Causeway, and strictly abide by local regulations barring the filming or sharing of attack sites and counter-missile activity.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is warning about voter turnout in the elections underway Tuesday.
"We're at war for our home 🚨," Netanyahu added in a second post. "Muslim Brotherhood supporters are raiding the polling stations and stealing the elections.
"Go out and vote, recover it!!"
Cars flying Netanyahu's Likud party flags drove through Jerusalem blaring the Islamic call to prayer and urging supporters to cast their ballots because "Arabs are voting," witnesses said.
"If we don't wake up now, we'll find ourselves with a government of Mansour Abbas and Ahmed Tibi," Netanyahu wrote in a post, referring to two leading Palestinian Arab politicians in Israel.
Turnout reached 55.7% in the first nine hours of voting, the elections committee said, the fastest pace on record.
Arabs, mostly of Palestinian heritage, make up about 21% of Israel's population of 10 million and have traditionally voted at lower rates than Jewish Israelis.
Tibi, a candidate from an Arab party, said strong turnout among Israel's Arab minority would "pave the way for an alternative government and change the grave reality."
Sami Abu Shehadeh, leader of the Arab Balad party, wrote on X that long lines outside polling stations should bring "pride and joy to anyone who believed in democracy."
"We are receiving all these inciting messages from the petty racists, Ben-Gvir, Netanyahu, and their partners," he added. " What are they afraid of ? This is actually an excellent sight, it is good for democracy."
In a statement, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir described the level of Arab voter turnout as "crazy," urging supporters to vote for his Jewish Power party if they wanted the country to be Jewish and Zionist .
Smotrich's Religious Zionism party said the finance minister had suspended his election day campaigning to convene an emergency meeting to discuss what it described as unusually high turnout among Arab voters.
Reuters contributed to this report.
President Donald Trump highlighted incoming shipments of Venezuelan crude Tuesday as a direct economic cushion against rising fuel prices spurred by the 9-month-old conflict with Iran, pointing to alternative energy imports during a campaign departure for Texas.
Speaking to reporters ahead of rallies alongside Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, Trump praised recent surges in consumer confidence before confirming plans to showcase an arriving oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude destined for processing at Gulf Coast facilities.
"We took over Venezuela very successfully, and they've sent me as a gift, a boatload of a million barrels of oil, and I'm giving that to the United States of America," Trump told reporters on the tarmac from Joint Base Andrews, framing the imports as a tangible benefit of his administration's pressure campaign.
"We're going to accept a million barrels of oil, and I'm going to give it to you people to use it the way you want. And we're going to have oil prices are going to be dropping very sharply."
The administration has increasingly relied on Western Hemisphere energy flows to offset global supply contractions caused by maritime blockades in the Strait of Hormuz and repeated strikes by Iran-aligned proxies on regional Gulf infrastructure.
With domestic pump prices edging above previous-term averages just a week before the November midterms, the White House has maintained that foreign oil seizures, increased Caribbean imports, and record domestic production will neutralize temporary spikes until the Middle East war is resolved.
House Budget Committee Chairman Jodey Arrington , R-Texas, strongly defended President Donald Trump's military confrontation with Tehran on Tuesday.
Arrington argued that decades of bipartisan caution had allowed Iran’s regional aggression to metastasize unchecked, insisting that Trump prioritized long-term American safety over near-term political risks.
"Look, we had a precipitous decline in the cost of energy leading up to the Iranian conflict," Arrington told FOX Business ' "Big Money in the Morning" on Tuesday.
"I think the American people understand that for almost 50 years, we gave that terrorist regime a pass. I think this president recognized that he was going to be the last commander in chief to address this situation before we had a Kim Jong Un in the Middle East, essentially.
"And so he was willing to take the risk, quite frankly. Thank God we have a commander in chief that's willing to do things that aren't in his political interest on account of the security interest of the American people."
Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash. , who stands to reclaim the chairmanship of the House Armed Services Committee if Democrats win the House majority in the upcoming midterm elections, signaled Tuesday that impeachment proceedings against War Secretary Pete Hegseth are firmly on the table.
"Well, I think we need to thoroughly investigate all of them to be sure, because there's been a lack of transparency at the Pentagon," Smith told CNN on Tuesday. "I think, we need the shine a brighter light on it and organize it, say, OK, these are the issues that are most concerning."
Smith pointed to the Republican-led push initiated before the pre-election recess by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., who introduced eight articles of impeachment targeting Hegseth 's execution of the Iran campaign under the War Powers Resolution.
With Massie preparing to reintroduce the privileged measure during the upcoming post-election session, a floor vote could occur within the next two weeks.
Because impeachment actions can carry over to a new Congress, approval during a lame-duck session could send the articles to the Senate for trial early next year.
"But then, as you know, right before we left, there was a Republican-led effort to impeach Pete Hegseth that, and I think that is definitely on the table," Smith added. "I think the way he has run the Pentagon has been shocking, not just to Democrats, but to a number of Republicans as well.
"So I've said a long, long time ago that he's not qualified for the job and he should be removed, and I think we're going to pursue that."
When asked directly whether he would vote to impeach the defense secretary, Smith replied:"I'd have to – in all likelihood, yes, but I have to look at the particular articles and the particular arguments before I make that commitment."

articles.title_orig: United ‘hijack’ text scare forces plane to turn back
articles.title_zh: United ‘hijack’ text scare forces plane to turn back
articles.content_orig:
The man is scheduled for an initial court appearance Tuesday.
LAS VEGAS -- An airplane passenger was arrested for allegedly writing a message while midair that he was going to “hijack” the plane, forcing the United flight to be diverted back to Las Vegas shortly after takeoff Saturday.
The 25-year-old allegedly communicated that he was “gonna hijack this” plane — although he used an expletive — and “crash ur row only,” according to a copy of the criminal complaint. The document doesn't specify exactly how the message was sent or to whom it was directed.
Las Vegas police said they detained the man after a report of a person making “terroristic threats” on the Saturday night flight that had been headed to Newark, New Jersey. He was arrested on charges of making a threat or providing false information regarding an act of terrorism, which carries a possible sentence of 1 to 20 years in prison.
An attorney listed for the man did not immediately return a request for comment. His initial court appearance is scheduled for Tuesday.
The scheduled redeye flight returned to the airport less than an hour after departing, according to Flightradar24 data.
United confirmed that the flight with 150 passengers on board returned safely to Las Vegas to address a “potential security concern.” The flight was delayed overnight and departed for Newark on Sunday morning.
The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed it will investigate the incident and said in an email to The Associated Press there have been over 1,400 unruly passenger incidents so far in 2026.

articles.title_orig: Chinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its toll
articles.title_zh: Chinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its toll
articles.content_orig:
Lack of profits and the threat posed by western countries are raising concern about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boom
Trillions of dollars have been wiped from China’s stock markets in recent months amid increasing anxiety about the future of artificial intelligence, as Beijing races against the United States for dominance in the sector.
The STAR 50 Index, which tracks technology and innovation companies on the Shanghai stock exchange, has plunged 40% since June. Other indexes of major companies dropped by about 20% over the same time period.
The precipitous drop has wiped out $2.4tn from the Chinese stock market since May, according to Bloomberg.
AI stocks account for over 40% of the stock market value in China and Hong Kong, according to Goldman Sachs, meaning that any dent in value will send shockwaves across the whole domestic market.
The fall suggests that despite the government’s best efforts to boost China’s technology industries, particularly those which harness the power of AI, the domestic economy does not have the power to sustain a booming market.
The Chinese government has invested heavily into AI, including a 60bn yuan state-backed AI investment fund which started pumping money into domestic developers this month. But Chinese consumers have proved stubbornly reluctant to part with their cash in many parts of the economy – including technology – meaning that many tech companies struggle to turn a profit.
The lack of profits is one of several reasons for the sell-off. Another is the threat of western countries, especially the US, extending bans on Chinese technology.
“This year, the profit margin is not as good as expected. And the US is raising rates. And China’s domestic demand is so weak,” said Dan Wang, the China director for the Eurasia Group. She said that there was a “general anxiety” among technology companies about whether or not the state-backed model would work in the face of weak consumer demand.
The US has banned humanoid robots from China , citing national security risks, and is thought to be considering a ban on Chinese components in data centres. China is heavily reliant on exports and restrictions in the US hurt its domestic companies, which struggle to sell enough products at home.
As China races with the US to pull ahead in AI, Beijing has doubled down on robotics – also known as embodied AI – as the key to rolling out the technology across society. Robotics is also seen as the answer to China’s demographic problems, such as the ageing population and the shrinking workforce.
But the demand for robotics is being driven by government agencies and research institutions, rather than everyday consumers, for whom the products are still too expensive and not yet practical for home use. Humanoid robotics and robotic dogs have been popular in the entertainment industry but are yet to be useful in home settings.
Shares in Unitree, China’s leading robot-maker, have halved since they started trading in August.
“It doesn’t look like embodied intelligence could turn into profits in the in the mass market,” said Wang. Thin profit margins, rising rates in the US, and weak domestic demand were all contributing to a “general anxiety” among technology companies, she said.
China’s government wants local investors to invest their money domestically. China has in recent months restricted overseas investment, with more regulations taking effect from 1 December, but these moves have not led to greater investment in the Chinese markets.
Wang added that there was still optimism in other technology sectors, such as AI research and satellites, the latter because their links to the military indicates long term state support for the sector. And globally the AI boom is expected to last for at least another year.
On Monday, US AI company Anthropic, which makes the chatbot Claude, filed paperwork ahead of a planned IPO that could be the biggest stock market debuts of all time. The company is expected to bring in as much as $100bn.
China has no such blockbuster IPOs on the horizon. And despite pressure on policymakers to introduce stimulus measures to boost investment, none are expected to be announced during a politically sensitive period in China.
This week the top officials in the Chinese Communist party are gathering for the fifth plenum , an important meeting that will lay the groundwork for next year’s 21st Party Congress. The Congress is expected to anoint Xi Jinping, China’s leader, for a fourth term. There is no appetite for risky or potentially destabilising policy measures before then, even if there is a chance they could boost the economy.
Any stimulus measure would be “high risk”, Wang said. “What if it doesn’t work out? Then whoever came up with that policy, that guy would be held accountable”.

articles.title_orig: S&P 500 rises as chip stocks gain for a second day, oil prices ease: Live updates
articles.title_zh: S&P 500 rises as chip stocks gain for a second day, oil prices ease: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
The S&P 500 rose on Tuesday as enthusiasm surrounding chipmakers led traders to move into the names for another day. Investors also monitored a slide in oil prices and parsed through a slew of corporate earnings as the Federal Reserve began its two-day policy meeting.
The broad market index was up 0.7%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 107 points, or 0.2%. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.3%.
Shares of Broadcom climbed more than 3% on the heels of a coalition of banks — namely, Bank of America , Citi and Morgan Stanley — and Blackstone announcing $63 billion in financing for the purchase of Broadcom's technology for Anthropic. Other chipmakers rose in sympathy. Micron Technology was up more than 1%, while Advanced Micro Devices advanced nearly 3%.
The latest moves in those stocks add to their gains from the prior trading day, which saw the major averages record a winning session , thanks in part to a boost in artificial intelligence-related stocks after Anthropic filed to go public at the Nasdaq. This would mark another major tech IPO for 2026, following SpaceX's blockbuster listing in June.
"The market has these kind of periodic interludes where it gets concerned about AI spending, and then we tend to go back and tech leads us higher," said Jed Ellerbroek, Argent Capital Management portfolio manager. "The light switch has been off for the last two weeks, and it looks like the first two days this week, the switch has been flipped up again."
Despite those recent concerns, Ellerbroek still sees "great" conviction from companies that own data centers to continue to grow. "The potential crack in the foundation remains just how volatile capital markets can be," he added.
A decline in oil prices also supported sentiment Tuesday. The moves came after Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei and his top national security official Mohsen Rezaei discussed the country's conditions for ending the conflict. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures were 1% lower to around $100 per barrel, while global benchmark Brent crude futures shed more than 1% to roughly $114 a barrel.
Meanwhile, JetBlue jumped 20% despite the airline posting a larger-than-expected third-quarter loss, as the company said it expects to see further margin expansion in the fourth quarter. UPS shares were marginally higher after the delivery giant reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter. On the flip side, Whirlpool dropped more than 1% after posting a surprise quarterly loss.
The Fed is set to kick off its latest monetary policy meeting Tuesday. While the central bank is expected to keep rates unchanged, traders will look for clues on whether another rate hike will take place before year-end.
"This feels like a rare Fed meeting non-event under Warsh. It feels like his communication strategy is going to result in fewer of these no-surprise meetings, but it it does look like we're going to get one here, mostly because the midterm election is next week," Ellerbroek also said. "I assume that next meeting in December is going to be another kind of live wire."
Stephens is initiating coverage on Mama's Creations with an overweight rating.
The firm put a $19 price target for the company, implying a 55% upside from Monday's close.
"MAMA has evolved from a single-brand meatball company into a scaled deli solutions platform, with three manufacturing facilities and a portfolio spanning beef, chicken, salads, olives and sides," wrote analyst Jim Salera.
Shares were last up around 3% in late morning trading on Tuesday.
Shares of SoFi Technologies were higher by more than 13% in early trading Tuesday after it reported stronger-than-expected financial results in the third quarter.
Revenue and earnings both beat estimates, according to FactSet, and adjusted EBITDA came in more than $40 million above expectations.
The fintech company raised guidance across all of those metrics for full-year 2026, and it delivered forecasts for 2027 that came in higher than estimates too.
"We had exceptional Q3 results against the backdrop of any environment," said SoFi CEO Anthony Noto in a news release. "But they are even more remarkable given how 2026 has unfolded."
A new $10 billion venture fund is aiming to capitalize on the growing security and defense requirements being propelled by artificial intelligence systems.
Disruptive Technology Advisers, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, will back "category-leading private technology companies," the company said in a release. The name of the fund is the Disruptive Flagship Fund.
The LLC, which was founded in 2012, foresees a "new era of investment in defense and national security" businesses, creating "companies of unprecedented scale and strategic importance."
"The firm has developed an investment model designed to identify a small number of exceptional companies and deploy significant capital behind them," Disruptive Technology Advisers said in a statement. The new fund will deploy up to $1 billion per company.
AI has made explicit forays into sensitive fields including cryptology , leading to consternation among mathematicians, though the security implications and resulting commercial possibilities are likely more widely ranging.
The three major averages moved higher shortly after the opening bell on Tuesday.
The S&P 500 gained 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 74 points, or 0.1%. The Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.5%.
Demand for long-lasting goods such as airplanes, defense equipment and household appliances rose sharply in September, the Commerce Department reported Tuesday.
Durable goods orders increased 1.8% for the period, up from a 0.1% increase in August and slightly better than the 1.7% consensus forecast from Dow Jones. Excluding transportation, orders increased 0.5%, while they jumped 2.2% when excluding defense.
Check out the companies making headlines before the bell:
Shares of Boeing rose nearly 1% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the company's third-quarter revenue beat analysts' expectations.
For the quarter, Boeing posted revenue of $24.19 billion, above the $23.84 billion that analysts surveyed by LSEG were expecting.
However, the company reported an adjusted loss of 34 cents per share versus the loss per share of 21 cents that analysts were anticipating.
UPS traded 1.3% higher after the delivery and logistics giant reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter.
The company earned an adjusted $1.69 per share on revenue of $22.9 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a profit of $1.63 per share on revenue of $22.29 billion.
UPS also hiked its full-year revenue guidance.
In-store inflation rose to its highest level in over two years this month, the British Retail Consortium said on Tuesday.
Shop price inflation reached 2.1% on an annual basis during Oct. 1 and Oct. 7, the BRC's figures showed, led by food inflation, which rose to 2.9%.
"The dam is starting to break on the huge wave of costs retailers have absorbed over the last two years," Helen Dickinson, CEO of the organization, said in a statement.
"The message to the Chancellor ahead of tomorrow's Budget could not be clearer: act now or prices will keep on rising," she added. "Without a change of course, October's jump in inflation is only the beginning."
U.K. finance minister John Healey is set to deliver his first Autumn Budget to parliament on Wednesday. The BRC is calling on the government to cut employment costs, reduce taxes on business premises and cut other duties imposed on shops.
French statistics agency Insee said Tuesday that consumer confidence had deteriorated significantly in October amid public unrest, rioting and demonstrations, falling to its lowest level since June 2013.
Optimism toward the future standard of living had seen a "clear downturn," Insee said, with an increase in fears about unemployment.
France is currently in the midst of a political crisis, as it seeks to simultaneously slash its national deficit and appease protesters

articles.title_orig: Nintendo Indie World Showcase set for October 28
articles.title_zh: Nintendo Indie World Showcase set for October 28
articles.content_orig:
Drop what you are doing. Nintendo just announced a new showcase for this week. We won't have to wait long to find out what the company has in store, as the new Indie World Showcase is being held tomorrow, Oct. 28. Unlike some of the bigger Directs we've seen recently, this will be a smaller affair. That doesn't mean you should miss it, however, as there are still plenty of potential surprises in store.
Thanks to Nintendo's official announcement , we know the latest Indie World Showcase will be roughly 15 minutes long. The showcase will be held at 7:00 a.m. PDT. You can watch it on Nintendo's YouTube channel . The company said that it will focus on "new announcements and updates on indie games coming to Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch."
While we've had a number of big Directs this year, the last Indie World Showcase was held back in March. That event had a number of exciting indies for Switch and Switch 2 owners, such as this year's amazing Denshattack! and the shadow drop of roguelite puzzler Blue Prince on Switch 2.
Since this is an indie-focused showcase, announcements will be from Nintendo's third-party partners. That means you shouldn't expect to see the likes of Zelda, Mario, or Samus, unless they appear in a project like Cadence of Hyrule . Instead, get ready to be introduced to several smaller titles coming in the next few months that are still worth your time alongside juggernauts like the Ocarina of Time remake .
While predicting what will be announced at an Indie World Showcase is a little harder than with a Direct, there is one thing we can all hope for. We know Team Cherry is working on an expansion to last year's game, Hollow Knight: Silksong , called Sea of Sorrow . It has been a while since the developer last shared information, but it was initially announced with a 2026 release date. It wouldn't be impossible for Team Cherry to shadow drop it, or at least reveal the expansion's actual release date. That is, of course, unless it is delayed.

articles.title_zh: Earnings live updates: Boeing stock falls on mixed Q3 turnaround picture, SoFi surges
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Third quarter earnings season is in full swing this week, with corporate results on deck from Big Tech heavy-hitters Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Amazon ( AMZN ).
Aside from Big Tech, industries from oil to chips to pharmaceuticals will be represented, as Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), Intel ( INTC ), Boeing ( BA ), Ford ( F ), and Eli Lilly ( LLY ) also open their books.
It's shaping up to be another strong earnings season. According to FactSet data , nearly a quarter of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings so far, with an overall earnings growth rate of 29.5%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
United Parcel Service ( UPS ) stock rose 2% on Tuesday after the courier posted third quarter results and raised its full-year guidance, signaling solid demand during the upcoming holiday season.
Revenue is expected to come in at $92.6 billion this year, up from a prior forecast of $91.2 billion. UPS also increased its adjusted earnings guidance.
Despite inflation pressures and high diesel costs, UPS is optimistic heading into the last few months of the year.
"US consumers remain resilient and the outlook for holiday demand is strong," CEO Carol Tomé said on the company's earnings call.
The company is in the middle of a multiyear turnaround plan aimed at cost-cutting and reconfiguring its delivery network.
JetBlue Airways ( JBLU ) shares rose more than 14% in premarket trading on Tuesday following the release of third-quarter results and guidance for 2027. The airline reported a loss per share of $0.60, compared to analyst estimates of $0.54. Revenue reached $2.81 billion, slightly below the $2.83 billion consensus estimate.
The airline posted an operating margin of negative 5.1% for the quarter. Operating revenue totaled $2.81 billion while operating expenses came in at $2.96 billion. The company's operating revenue increased 21% year-over-year.
Chief Executive Officer Joanna Geraghty said resilient demand and strong yields drove revenue ahead of initial expectations, allowing the company to offset more of the fuel cost increases than anticipated. She noted that Fort Lauderdale continues to deliver strong results even as the company grows capacity in that market.
Yahoo Finance's Brooke DiPalma reports:
Coca-Cola ( KO ) posted better-than-expected third quarter results and raised its earnings outlook, but the company saw slowing demand in its North American business.
Coca-Cola stock traded lower in early trading.
The company posted adjusted earnings of $0.91 per share, above the $0.88 expected by Wall Street analysts, alongside revenue of $13.4 billion, also higher than estimates of $12.9 billion.
Overall unit case volume grew by 5%, more than the roughly 3% expected. The increase was once again led by Coke Zero, which grew roughly 16% year over year. Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Light grew by 6%.
Boeing ( BA ) shrank its quarterly losses and generated cash flow in the third quarter, but its top- and bottom-line results missed Wall Street's expectations.
Revenue of $24.1 billion and an adjusted loss per share of $0.34 came in below estimates of revenue of $24.3 billion and a loss of $0.20 per share.
The company's commercial airplane unit faced higher costs in its supply chain and for production as well as a $700 million charge on its 777X program. As a result, its operating margin in that segment fell to -6.5%.
"Backlog reached a record $745B. The 737-7 and 737-10 FAA certifications and F/A-XX award are meaningful milestones, though BCA margin deterioration to -6.5% from Q2's -2.7% introduces uncertainty around the recovery pace," CFRA analysts wrote in a note following the results.
SoFi ( SOFI ) stock surged 10% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the online financial services provider lifted its 2026 outlook and reported strong results for the third quarter.
Here's what SoFi reported for Q3, compared to Wall Street analyst estimates compiled by S&P Market Intelligence:
Revenue: up 45.9% year over year to $1.39 billion, above estimates of $1.26 billion.
Adjusted earnings: $0.18, above estimates of $0.17.
Updated 2026 guidance: SoFi now expects net revenue of $5.04 billion in 2026, reflecting a 40% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA is now expected at $1.66 billion of adjusted EBITDA, and earnings per share are forecast at $0.61. Wall Street analysts were expecting 2026 earnings per share of $0.59.
The company also introduced 2027 guidance, guiding for $0.90 of earnings per share, which is above the Street's estimate of $ 0.82.
"We had exceptional Q3 results against the backdrop of any environment, but they are even more remarkable given how 2026 has unfolded," CEO Anthony Noto said. "Our focus is simple. We are adding more members, who are using more products, and generating more revenue per product to create the most value for our shareholders over the long run. In less than a decade, we have transformed SoFi from a single-product company into an everything financial app with eight different businesses each generating over $100 million in annualized revenue."
Whirlpool posted another mixed quarter as inflation and lower demand in North America took a toll.
"What is new and different is the increasingly inflationary environment that has happened from Q2 into Q3, as well as the impact of volume deleveraging which is driven by the softer demand that we have in the North America industry," Whirlpool CFO Roxanne Warner told Yahoo Finance, adding that the team is focusing on what it can control.
In the third quarter, the company reported revenue declined by nearly 9% to $3.68 billion, which was below estimates of $3.91 billion. The company reported an adjusted loss per share of $0.21, lower than the adjusted earnings per share estimate of $0.76,  per Bloomberg consensus data
Warner said that the industry hasn't caught up to the "full impact of the inflationary pressures from 2022," with inflation up 12% since then.
For that reason,  the company plans to raise prices for the third time this year, now by 7% in the fourth quarter. That follows its largest price increase in history in April, at 10%, and a 4% increase in its list prices in July.
Revenue for major appliances in its North America business fell 8.3% year over year to $2.5 billion, below Wall Street's expectations.
Whirlpool's small domestic appliance business fell almost 1% to $286 million, below the expected $314 million. However, the company said that in the third quarter, some items sold out, leading to roughly 40% year-over-year growth in US orders in October.

What to know about the Iran war:
An oil tanker has caught fire after being caught in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy said on Tuesday.
"Hours ago, a rogue oil tanker that had switched off its tracking systems and was attempting to pass through a prohibited and unsafe area east of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines, sustaining damage and catching fire," the navy's public relations office said.
"The Strait of Hormuz is unsafe and closed to rogue ships and vessels attempting to pass through without coordination," it added.
Iran has repeatedly said it will only allow vessels to pass through the waterway if they coordinate with authorities. The U.S. has urged shippers to use a southern route through the strait that Tehran regards as illegal.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is in "perfect health," describing him as energetic, hopeful and composed following a meeting.
Khamenei was seriously wounded in the strikes that killed his father, Ali Khamenei, sources told CBS News in March. He has not been seen in public since the start of the war.
"The leader is in perfect health, and truly, what I observed during the meeting was a strong, energetic, hopeful and resolute spirit, along with inner peace," Ghalibaf said Tuesday.
"These qualities were fully evident in the leader," he added, "and I felt with all my being that this resolve and inner peace reflect a strong faith in Almighty God and a deep belief in the people."

"Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi group toward the capital, Riyadh," spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki wrote in a post on X .
Multiple explosions were heard in Riyadh on Tuesday, journalists from the AFP news agency said.
Residents received a text-message alert on their mobile phones warning of an "aerial threat" and instructing them to seek shelter.
This latest attack follows weeks of strikes by the Houthis, who claimed Tuesday to have struck a refinery in eastern Saudi Arabia.
A Kuwaiti State Security and Terrorism Criminal Court sentenced three men to death on Monday over an alleged plot to assassinate First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef, with prosecutors accusing the defendants of spying for Iran, communicating with Iranian-linked entities and joining Hezbollah, two judicial sources told the AFP news agency Tuesday.
The court also sentenced eight other defendants to varying prison terms.
Those sentenced to death included cleric and National Islamic Alliance Secretary-General Hussein Abdullah Al-Maatouq and two other men. One of the defendants had previously been convicted of terrorism in 2016 and later received a pardon before being arrested again in April, the sources said.
According to Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Rai , the defendants were accused of communicating with Iran and entities allegedly operating in its interests, including Lebanese group Hezbollah, to carry out hostile acts against Kuwait following the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on Feb. 28, at the beginning of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.
The defendants were also accused of joining Hezbollah, a banned group in Kuwait, while knowing its objectives, and of engaging in activities allegedly intended to undermine the country's political, social and economic order and harm its national interests.
Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Qabas reported prosecutors accused the defendants of attempting to use explosives to carry out the alleged assassination plot and spread panic. One defendant was separately accused of attempting to bring explosives into the country to enable the others to carry out the alleged operation.
The reported Iran connection forms a central part of the case, although the allegations against the defendants do not, on their own, establish that the Iranian government directed the alleged assassination plot.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed Tuesday to have struck a refinery in eastern Saudi Arabia.
"With the help of Almighty God, the Yemeni Armed Forces succeeded in targeting the Ras Tanura refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile," military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said in a post on X .
"The strike was accurate," he added, "and caused massive fires at the targeted site."
The alleged strike follows weeks of Houthi attacks against the world's top exporter of crude oil.
A resident in the nearby city of Al Khobar told the AFP news agency he heard explosions around dawn and then received a warning message on his phone.
"We got the alert on the mobile and then heard a very loud bang," the resident said.
The Ras Tanura facility along Saudi Arabia's eastern Gulf coast is home to one of the largest refineries in the Middle East and is a cornerstone of the kingdom's energy sector.
The complex has a capacity to refine 550,000 barrels per day. It has been repeatedly targeted by Iranian strikes, including a drone attack in early March that forced a partial shutdown of the refinery.

Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, and Nouman Essghir, 24, both British nationals and London residents, were charged under the 2023 National Security Act.
Abdulkarim was charged with "assisting a foreign intelligence service" in September and "engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out U.K.-related activities."
The CPS said Essghir was charged with a national security offense after he "approached or was in the vicinity of a prohibited place and his conduct was for a purpose that he knew, or having regards to other matters known to him ought reasonably to have known, was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom."
Both men were arrested last week on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service in a suspected plot targeting the Fairford air base in England.
The U.S. embassy in Baghdad has shot down two drones, Saudi state television channel Al Arabya reported Tuesday.
An Iraqi security source told the outlet that air defenses protecting the embassy destroyed the drones.
The government-owned Iraqi television channel Al-Anbar reported that the head of Iraq's Security Media Cell, Saad Maan, said that explosions heard across the capital were the result of a drone being intercepted and shot down.
The drone's origin remains unknown, and no immediate reports of casualties or damage have been released. The U.S. State Department has not yet commented on the incident.
An oil slick in the Gulf has reached a beach in the United Arab Emirates, video from the AFP news agency showed on Tuesday, with experts warning it could threaten desalination plants as it spreads.
UAE authorities said Friday that they had "detected a tanker oil spill affecting Umm Al Quwain's beaches," referring to an emirate north of Dubai.
By Tuesday morning, footage shot by AFP showed workers cleaning up oil on the emirate's beaches, which had been shut earlier by authorities along with other beaches in the country.
Satellite images taken on Oct. 21 and analyzed by AFP show what appears to be a slick of about 70 square miles in that area. Three days later, images showed it had quadrupled in size to around 290 square miles.
Experts from NGOs including Dutch peace group PAX said oil came from the tanker GEM NO.2 after it was attacked on Oct. 9.
They warned the slick could affect operations at UAE desalination plants, crucial for supplying water to the Gulf country.

On Monday, Verizon Communications Inc. (NYSE: VZ ) CEO Dan Schulman sees opportunities to collaborate with satellite providers such as Elon Musk's Starlink , but says the wireless carrier has no reason to let Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ: SPCX ) use its network to compete for mobile customers .
Speaking during Verizon's third-quarter earnings call, Schulman acknowledged that satellite connectivity could complement traditional wireless services, particularly in remote areas with limited cellular coverage.
"I do think there is a role for satellite for sure in remote areas. It's a great service for those customers," he said, adding, "And I do think there are ways that we can work together, either directly or through our JV with satellite providers, to provide a complementary service and a differentiated value proposition."
Schulman reiterated that the company has no plans to offer satellite providers access to its network through mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) agreements.
"I will say, and I'll repeat it again, that there are no backdoors to any of our MVNO agreements and I see absolutely no benefit whatsoever to extending an MVNO deal to any satellite provider," he added.
An MVNO, or mobile virtual network operator, sells wireless services using another carrier's network rather than relying entirely on its own infrastructure.
Read Also: Dow Surges Over 200 Points; Verizon Shares Fall Following Q3 Results
During the call, Schulman said Verizon takes SpaceX's ambitions seriously and assumes the company will execute its plans successfully.
He argued that competing directly with established wireless carriers would require SpaceX to build a substantial terrestrial network, including 65,000 to 80,000 macro sites, backhaul infrastructure, radio access equipment and significant spectrum resources.
Schulman estimated that such a buildout could take at least four to six years and cost $300 billion to $500 billion over seven to eight years.
He also dismissed the idea that Verizon must offer Starlink network access to prevent rivals from gaining an advantage.
"There is no benefit to Verizon Communications extending an MVNO deal," Schulman said, adding that the company intends to compete aggressively if SpaceX enters the market. "We will punch back hard when that happens," he said.
Verizon shares closed down 3.49% at $43.10 on Monday, despite the company reporting its strongest third-quarter wireless subscriber growth in five years, beating earnings expectations and raising its full-year outlook.
