articles.title_orig: Apple Creator Studio gets powerful new AI features using OpenAI models
articles.title_zh: Apple Creator Studio gets powerful new AI features using OpenAI models
articles.content_orig:
Apple Creator Studio updates have today been announced, with what the company describes as “powerful new AI features” using a combination of Apple Intelligence and OpenAI models.
Final Cut Pro for Mac will also include built-in MotionVFX to provide a large collection of visual effects, transitions, and motion graphics tools …
Apple announced the updates alongside the new iMacs and 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip. It will be a free update for existing subscribers at some point in November.
Final Cut Pro for Mac now includes built-in MotionVFX — an expansive collection of visual effects, plug-ins, transitions, templates, and motion graphics tools — as well as seamless editing in Pixelmator Pro. Apple’s curated Content Hub now includes video assets and is available in Final Cut Pro.
Music creators using Logic Pro for Mac gain a new intelligent assistant in beta, an enhanced Stem Splitter that now separates drums, and a redesigned Browser that incorporates all sounds, with music understanding and even a Splice library.
Pixelmator Pro introduces Generate Fill, which lets creators transform selected areas of an image using natural language.
Keynote, Pages, and Numbers introduce new AI features in beta, including assistants 2 that understand document context and new Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for workflow automation. They also add stock video in the Content Hub and new premium themes and templates.
The headline news here is MotionVFX for Final Cut Pro.
Final Cut Pro for Mac now integrates MotionVFX directly into the app, giving editors access to thousands of elements, including templates with unique themes, stylish graphics, titles, and transitions, as well as tools for rotoscoping, tracking, and color grading. Editors can also tap into the Content Hub directly within Final Cut Pro and access a library of Apple-curated stock videos, photos, and backgrounds to fill gaps, add polish, or spark new ideas without leaving their workflow.
Also notable is that the inclusion of OpenAI models alongside Apple Intelligence.
A new intelligent assistant powered by a combination of Apple-built models and OpenAI joins Logic Pro for Mac, helping creators and producers navigate production workflows, start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refine an active project.
Visual productivity apps receive a new generation of intelligence features for subscribers, including an intelligent assistant, built on Apple models and OpenAI, directly within Keynote, Pages, and Numbers. The assistant understands document context to help users accomplish more without leaving their work.
In Keynote, the intelligent assistant helps with designing, animating, and refining slides. In Pages, it drafts, restructures, and fine-tunes written content. In Numbers, it calculates, visualizes, and organizes data; recommends suitable chart types with a one-tap preview; and builds custom tables using world knowledge.
New MCP support, built on this platform, enables external AI agents and tools to read content, perform edits, and execute automated actions directly in Keynote, Pages, and Numbers.
Apple hasn’t announced an exact launch date for the new features, instead saying that it will be “this November.”

articles.title_orig: Microsoft Issues Emergency Patch For Critical Google Algorithm Flaw
articles.title_zh: Microsoft Issues Emergency Patch For Critical Google Algorithm Flaw
articles.content_orig:
CVE-2026-111497: Critical out-of-bounds write in the Node.js Brotli decoder
CVE-2026-111497: Critical out-of-bounds write in the Node.js Brotli decoder
On October 21, 2026, the Node.js Project published a security advisory for CVE-2026-111497 , an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js. The vulnerability affects the Node.js 26.x , 24.x , and 22.x release lines. Node.js rates the issue High, while Google, the CVE Numbering Authority (CNA), gives it a critical CVSSv4 score of 9.2 .
An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with node:zlib can corrupt process memory. According to Node.js, this corruption can lead to a process crash, disclosure of sensitive process memory, or remote code execution. Exposure therefore depends on whether an application passes attacker-controlled compressed data to the affected decoder.
As of October 26, 2026, Rapid7 is not aware of exploitation in the wild, and CVE-2026-111497 is not listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog . However, given the vulnerability's potential to disclose memory or enable remote code execution (RCE), Rapid7 recommends that organizations prioritize remediation.
CVE-2026-111497 is classified as an out-of-bounds write ( CWE-787 ) and an unchecked return value ( CWE-252 ). Per the vendor advisory, the decoder handled an invalid Brotli block switch as a temporary need for more input instead of a permanent format error. The streaming decoder then continued appending input bytes to an eight-byte internal buffer, allowing malformed input to write beyond the buffer and corrupt process memory.
The vulnerability originates in Google Brotli, which the affected Node.js release lines bundle as a dependency. The CVE record identifies affected upstream Brotli ranges on all platforms as versions 1.0.3 before 1.0.10 , 1.1.0 before 1.1.1 , and 1.2.0 before 1.2.1 . The Node.js Project remediated its bundled decoder in the fixed Node.js releases listed below.
Because CVE-2026-111497 affects the upstream Google Brotli decoder, its reach is not limited to Node.js. Vendor and project advisories have also identified affected implementations in Bun , Python's Brotli and brotlicffi packages, .NET , Envoy and Istio , brotli4j , and operating-system packages . Affected versions, default exposure, and remediation vary by product; the presence of an affected decoder does not by itself establish exposure unless an application processes attacker-controlled Brotli data. Organizations should consult the relevant downstream vendor or distribution advisories to identify affected versions, assess exposure, and determine appropriate remediation.
Vendor-supplied security updates are available to remediate CVE-2026-111497. Organizations running an affected Node.js release should upgrade on an urgent basis, outside of normal patch cycles:
Node.js 22.x releases before 22.23.4 are affected; upgrade to 22.23.4 or later.
Node.js 24.x releases before 24.22.1 are affected; upgrade to 24.22.1 or later.
Node.js 26.x releases before 26.12.1 are affected; upgrade to 26.12.1 or later.
The vendor states that end-of-life Node.js release lines should also be treated as affected when a security release occurs. Organizations using an end-of-life release should migrate to a supported, fixed release line. Node.js has not published a vendor-supported workaround; if an immediate upgrade is not possible, Rapid7 recommends restricting or disabling application paths that decompress untrusted Brotli data as a temporary exposure-reduction measure.
For the latest mitigation guidance, please refer to the Node.js security advisory .
Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose customers can assess exposure to CVE-2026-111497 with an authenticated Linux and macOS vulnerability check expected to be available in the October 26 content release. Windows-based vulnerability check is in progress and an update will be provided soon. Please refer to this blog for the latest information.

General Motors announced Tuesday that it will transfer its stock listing from the New York Stock Exchange to Nasdaq next month, a move the Detroit automaker said reflects its growing focus on technology and innovation.
The company said its shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Nov. 17 under the existing ticker symbol "GM."
"GM's customer-focused, technology-driven strategy is creating value for our stockholders, making Nasdaq a natural home for our listing as we grow," GM Chief Financial Officer Paul Jacobson said in a statement. "We're grateful for our long-standing partnership with the New York Stock Exchange and its remarkable legacy."
GM, which operates the Chevrolet, Buick, GMC and Cadillac brands, has increasingly emphasized advanced vehicle technology as a key part of its long-term growth strategy.

The transfer could make GM eligible for inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index, which tracks 100 of the largest non-financial companies listed on the exchange, but inclusion is not guaranteed.

articles.title_orig: Citi AAdvantage Platinum & Business Card Changes: Higher Fee, New Benefits
articles.title_zh: Citi AAdvantage Platinum & Business Card Changes: Higher Fee, New Benefits
articles.content_orig:
Citi and American Airlines have a co-branded credit card agreement, which includes five cards issued in the United States. It has just been announced that we’ll see changes to the mid-range personal and business cards — we’re talking the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select World Elite Mastercard and the Citi AAdvantage Business World Elite Mastercard.
The cards are getting some new benefits, though the annual fees will also be increased. Let’s cover the details, and let me emphasize that there are no changes to the no annual fee Citi AAdvantage MileUp Card, or the premium Citi AAdvantage Globe Card and Citi AAdvantage Executive Card.
Let’s start with the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Card, which has historically had a $99 annual fee, waived the first year. The card’s annual fee will be increasing to $150, though the card will also be getting all kinds of new benefits . Here are the new benefits being added to the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Card:
These changes are in addition to the current Citi AAdvantage Platinum Card benefits, which include the following:
Next, let’s cover the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, which has historically had a $99 annual fee, waived the first year. The card’s annual fee will be increasing to $150, though the card will also be getting all kinds of new benefits . Here are the new benefits being added to the Citi AAdvantage Business Card:
These changes are in addition to the current Citi AAdvantage Business Card benefits, which include the following:
While these changes apply effective immediately for new applicants, existing cardmembers won’t immediately see the changes. Beginning January 24, 2027, existing cardmembers (on both the personal and business card) will have access to the new benefits. They’ll also be billed the new $150 annual fee on their next account anniversary after that date.
Essentially we’re seeing the annual fees on American’s two mid-range cards increase by $51 per year, and I’d say we’re seeing three primary improvements. Those include a $100 annual inflight credit, a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit every four years, and much better travel coverage.
Obviously I’m not a fan of credit card annual fee inflation, and of the general trend of cards with sub-$100 annual fees becoming more expensive.
However, I generally think that if you found either card worthwhile before, you’ll probably still find it worthwhile after. At the same time, I don’t necessarily think these changes will make the card materially more appealing for anyone. So I’d view these as being pretty balanced and reasonable changes, even though I wish we weren’t seeing a fee hike. Then again, the cards have had these same types of fees for years, so the price increase basically just matches inflation.
Random thought — with all the American cards adding new inflight credits, I sure wish American would actually improve its selection of drinks and snacks for purchase, including shortening the minimum length of flight for items to be for sale. Actually using these credits just isn’t easy at times.
American Airlines and Citi are making changes to their co-brand credit card portfolio, particularly impacting the Platinum and Business products. Both cards will be seeing annual fees increase from $99 to $150, while getting new perks, including new bonus categories on spending, a $100 annual inflight credit, a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit, and improved travel coverage.
I’d probably view these changes as broadly being “breakeven,” in terms of the overall value propositions. I’m not a fan of the fee increase, but I also don’t think the value proposition is getting worse here, assuming you’re someone who values either card as is.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic IPO Filing Calms Nerves With Signs of Healthy Growth
articles.title_zh: Anthropic IPO Filing Calms Nerves With Signs of Healthy Growth
articles.content_orig:
The tech industry needs this to go well. So does Wall Street.
Anthropic's IPO filing on Monday puts the Claude creator in position to pursue what could be the largest initial stock offering in history. Investors are already measuring the 5-year-old company's potential market cap in the trillions, putting it in a category with the world's most valuable companies.
It's a critical moment for the whole tech sector, as the artificial intelligence boom has been largely driven by two companies: Anthropic and OpenAI. The latter has confidentially filed to go public, but has said a debut likely won't take place until 2027.
Meanwhile, the stock market is showing signs of jitters on the AI trade. Neoclouds and data center companies have been getting pummeled, prompting Australia's Firmus to withdraw its IPO plans and for SK Hynix's U.S.-based Solidigm unit to do the same.
Now, all eyes turn to Anthropic , which is betting that investors will look past over $80 billion in losses in the first half of the year, and see the 14-fold increase in revenue as a reflection of seemingly insatiable demand for the company's leading models and services.
"If it underperforms expectations, it'll be a little bit of a house of cards," said Jai Das, co-founder of Sapphire Ventures whose career in tech investing dates to the 1990s.
Anthropic's business is deeply entwined with tech megacaps. Close to half its revenue comes from Claude being sold through cloud divisions at Microsoft , Amazon and Alphabet , which all hold investments in the company. In the IPO, some $77 billion in notes can be issued to Amazon , Broadcom and Google , while Microsoft and Nvidia agreed to invest $15 billion as the company builds up its computing capacity. Chips from Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices , Amazon and Google are powering Anthropic's development.
Cloud providers are ratcheting up capital expenditures to meet demand, and memory manufacturers are fighting shortages to prioritize AI chips. And there's the debt factor. Alphabet, with its investment-grade credit rating, committed to backstopping Anthropic for a data center in Texas. Broadcom , which helps Google develop chips for AI labs, is creating financing pools to help Anthropic and OpenAI deploy high-performance models, CEO Hock Tan told analysts earlier this year.
For public market investors, more than one-third of the value of the S&P 500 comes from tech's trillion-dollar companies, which are all, to varying degrees, going deep in AI. Beyond that, there are software giants like Adobe and Salesforce that have integrated with Anthropic's Claude assistant.
And in the private markets, check sizes have ballooned but IPOs are few and far between. Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures both told CNBC that Anthropic is their biggest investment ever.
"If they don't perform well, they will become the bellwether for AI," said Brad Bernstein, a managing partner at growth equity firm FTV Capital. "Their valuation will reflect that performance variation, and then it'll just be a trickle-down effect to all the stuff going on with the excess capital that's getting poured into the venture AI world. Everything is going to have to sort of be reset."
Anthropic will be the third company to go public with a valuation above $1 trillion, after Saudi Aramco and Elon Musk's SpaceX , which debuted in June. OpenAI could be the fourth.
Revenue at Anthropic has been multiplying at a staggering pace as businesses adopt the company's coding and productivity tools. Second-quarter revenue soared to $11.56 billion from $787 million a year earlier.
The company held almost $132 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term investments at the end of June. And after five quarters of operating losses, Anthropic reported $974 million in operating income for the second quarter.
"It is, I think, better than feared," said Rohit Kulkarni, partner and chief AI officer at Burnham Park Capital Markets, referring to the financials. "There could have been more negative tidbits."
One source of concern in some corners of the investing universe is the emergence of so-called open-weight models, which are cheaper for businesses to access and allow for customization and flexibility in terms of where users access the models.
In the prospectus, the only two competitors Anthropic named were OpenAI and Google, though the company said it faces competition from a "broader set of model providers," including open-weight or open-source models.
Anthropic says it's all very early, with Fortune 500 companies committing less than 0.1% of their total expenses to its models and services in the latest quarter. Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs, says that's part of the investment thesis.
"I think there's going to be room for frontier models like Anthropic and OpenAI and SpaceX, and I think there will be room for open-weight models," Monaghan said. "It's way too soon to say that one is going to disintermediate the other."
With hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure set to reach into the trillions of dollars, Sapphire's Das said there's understandable concern about a market glut. But he compares it to the telecommunications and dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, when companies flooded the market with fiber-optic equipment. Eventually, the infrastructure got used, although plenty of companies went belly up in the interim.
"Long term, I don't think there is a lack of demand," Das said.
A lackluster debut could push out OpenAI's offering even further and cause investors to rethink its lofty valuation. At the same time, rising interest rates mean it's getting costlier for companies to raise debt.
David Trainer, CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, wrote in a report last month that the AI boom has been built on the view that cheap credit and access to the capital markets will be "readily available."
"If AI liquidity dries up, and there are clear signs it is, we see large, 20%, downside risk in the S&P 500, with most of that concentrated in the valuation of AI-related stocks," Trainer wrote.
Industry experts take a different approach, focusing on the power and rapid proliferation of the technology. Claude Opus 5.5 Max performs better than any other model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an industry benchmark .
Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said the technology is only becoming more essential.
"Anthropic and OpenAI have by now demonstrated their ability to stay at the frontier of AI and keep pushing innovation," Ramaswamy said. "They're incredible companies that are doing a big service to humanity by expanding the frontier of what is possible, and we are very much rooting for them to be public and very successful companies."
Still, Snowflake is experimenting with low-cost open-weight models from China's Moonshot AI, DeepSeek and Zhipu.
"We spend a lot on internal AI because we want to get as much efficiency as we can," Ramaswamy said.

articles.title_orig: Ford’s sub-$30K electric truck puts the home backup inverter right inside the vehicle
articles.title_zh: Ford’s sub-$30K electric truck puts the home backup inverter right inside the vehicle
articles.content_orig:
Owners of the Ford Fathom, starting at under $ 30 , 000 , can power their homes without buying a costly bidirectional charger. Will other automakers follow?
An artist’s rendering of the charging station and home backup panel that will be compatible with the Ford Fathom electric pickup truck’s alternating current–capable bidirectional charging system. (Ford)
Electric vehicles can serve as home backup batteries. But so far, most EVs have needed expensive bidirectional chargers to do that — a tough sell for customers.
Ford aims to remove this cost obstacle with its forthcoming Ford Fathom electric pickup truck . On Tuesday, the U.S. automaker revealed that the Fathom, which is set to retail at a starting price of $ 28 , 350 sometime next year, will be able to send power back to homes it’s plugged into without the same costly power-conversion tech that Ford’s now-discontinued F- 150 Lightning , and almost every other bidirectional-capable EV on the market, now requires.
Instead, the Fathom will come equipped with an onboard inverter that can convert its direct-current battery power to home-ready alternating current and deliver it via much cheaper equipment.
Today, most EVs sold in the U.S. lack that capability, instead requiring a DC-to-AC inverter device connected to the home. That gear now costs from just under $ 7 , 000 to more than $ 10 , 000 — a significant price barrier.
Ford hasn’t yet finalized the exact sum for the home power management tech that will work with the Fathom, but confirmed that it will be a lot cheaper than what’s available today.
“ One of the most central points of this whole story is the cost piece,” Dave McCreadie, Ford’s director of grid and energy services, told Canary Media in a Monday interview. ​ “ In order to see the adoption rate increase, reduced cost is a big piece of it, not just with the vehicle itself but the charging equipment — and now in this case, the discharging equipment.”
Specifically, Ford said that the new AC-capable bidirectional charger compatible with the Fathom will be roughly half the $ 1 , 300 price of the Ford Charge Station Pro, the bidirectional charging system it developed for the F- 150 Lightning. Both pieces of equipment allow homes to manage their power consumption when the grid remains up and running.
To back up their homes during grid outages, customers also need to purchase a home backup power panel. That tech combo will cost 60 % less than the $ 5 , 200 that the Ford Charge Station Pro combined with a home integration system does. (Note: These prices do not include installation costs.)
“ This is not going to be Ford’s last EV that is bidirectional capable,” McCreadie added. Other vehicles being produced based on Ford’s Universal EV Platform — the new technology line coming out of its retooled Louisville, Kentucky, factory — will also come with AC bidirectional charging capability, he said.
Right now, the only other EV models sold in the U.S. that come equipped to send AC power back to chargers are built by Tesla. The company’s Cybertruck has been AC-to-home capable for more than a year , and earlier this month, Tesla announced its latest Model 3 and Model Y vehicles can send AC power back to homes equipped with Tesla’s Powerwall batteries .
But the Fathom is a lot cheaper than Tesla’s EVs, and its system doesn’t require costly backup batteries. Meanwhile, DC-based systems from rivals such as General Motors, which makes a number of EVs capable of vehicle-to-home charging, are significantly more expensive — GM ’s sale price for its DC V 2 H bundle is $ 6 , 748 .
If AC bidirectional charging is so much cheaper, why haven’t more automakers made it available? The reasons boil down to the cost and complexity of enabling EVs to convert their native DC battery power to home-ready AC , along with the uncertain regulatory environment that would allow customers to adopt the technology en masse.
Ford’s onboard inverter tech for the Fathom and the Universal EV platform was developed in partnership with engineers at Auto Motive Power ( AMP ), a startup it acquired in 2023 . Jiaqi Liang, AMP ’s former vice president of hardware and now senior director of electrical hardware for Ford’s Advanced Programs team, said the cost of embedding a grid-ready inverter capability in EVs is relatively low.
“ The key here is to do it from scratch, so you don’t have the legacy-platform constraint,” he said. ​ “ We had the luxury of doing that from the Universal EV platform. It’s all integrated, from charging to discharging.”
To ensure that the AC power flowing from EVs is safe for homes, Ford’s system uses communications technology from a tech standard certified by the automotive standards organization SAE International called SAE J 3068 .
University of Delaware professor Willett Kempton led the development of the AC bidirectional charging capabilities for the J 3068 standard along with Rodney McGee, the university’s EV standards expert.
Embedding power conversion tech in an EV ​ “ gives any automaker the ability to have the car and the backup power system in the house communicate all the things you need to for safety,” Kempton explained in a Monday interview.
With that technology in place, the cost of enabling an EV to provide AC power is ​ “ in the $ 200 to $ 300 range,” he said — if it’s designed into the vehicle from the get-go. ​ “ If you want to add it on afterwards, it’s much more.”
Kempton is hopeful that additional automakers will choose to embed AC bidirectional capabilities in their EVs. ​ “ I talk with other automakers. They’re interested,” he said. ​ “ But when one of their peers announces ​ ‘ This is what we’re doing, and we’ll be 60 % cheaper,’ … I think that will have a big effect.”
The other challenge is to get utilities to allow AC bidirectional charging. Only California and Maryland have set utility regulations for AC bidirectional charging outside of pilot projects, and most of the country’s 3 , 000 -plus utilities have a ​ “ patchwork of rules and procedures” that complicate matters, McCreadie said.
Ford has been engaging with utilities and regulators in states including Michigan and Colorado to adopt clear guidelines for how vehicle-to-home charging can fit in with utility regulations. On Tuesday, it announced that it has been working since July with major utilities American Electric Power, BC Hydro, Consumers Energy, Exelon, and Pacific Gas & Electric to set common standards for how its AC V 2 H system can be integrated into standard utility interconnection rules.
“ We want to make sure that our customers interested in deploying this technology in their homes can get their system interconnected in the lowest-hassle way,” McCreadie said.

articles.content_orig:

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey is vowing to bring computer manufacturing back to the U.S. And by that, he doesn’t just mean assembly, but the production of every individual component, some of which are exclusively made in China today.
Anduril is partnering with Qualcomm to achieve that mission with a new computer called BlueChip, the companies announced Tuesday. BlueChip will be available for preorder in 2027.
While technical details are scant — Anduril hasn’t even finished contracting with all its component suppliers yet, according to Luckey — this first product will be a hardened laptop. It will be designed to withstand the most grueling physical environments and meet the security-conscious needs of the military, government, first responders and law enforcement.
For the first generation, about 90% of its components will be made in the U.S. or in allied countries, Anduril says, most notably its CPU. BlueChip will run on a Snapdragon X Series built at TSCM’s massive new facility in Arizona. The CPU uses the same architecture that powers other laptops, including the Microsoft Surface, Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said during the press conference.
“As of right now, the laptop’s bill of materials is about 90% U.S. and allied [ally countries], and we have a technical roadmap to get to 100% domestic over time,” Luckey said. “The intent in the long run is to have an option that is made entirely in the United States, 100% domestic. And I mean everything. I mean the displays. I mean the metallics. I mean the the magnetics. All of it.”
Right now, for instance, Luckey says he’s found an American supplier for the glass that covers the display, but the display itself is one of several components he says are only manufactured in China.
While Luckey says consumers are welcome to order a BlueChip — the company may even create a waiting list for interested consumers — this first PC won’t be designed for them. For one thing, as a hardened computer, it will be heavy and have battery-life constraints because of the engineering required to  withstand rain, dust, and other rugged conditions.
The bigger point is to offer U.S. government agencies a product that complies with regulations requiring them to buy U.S.-made computers. In this case, the selling point is a transparent supply chain that customers can track and audit.
“These computers are the anti-surveillance computer. You fully control it,” Luckey described in a recent interview. “You know everything that is in it, every single component, and you know every software component that is running on it.”
Anduril is also working to ensure that the Arm-based machine works well with Windows apps, apps built for certain Linux distributions used by the government, and even archaic software that various agencies still run.
While Anduril hasn’t yet announced pricing, Luckey estimates it will cost about 20% more than typical high-end PCs.
“As much as I love BlueChip, if I was just a normal consumer making a rational decision without a kind of patriotic basis, I’d be better off buying a Dell laptop than an Anduril laptop because it’s going to be cheaper. I’m just talking about your average person consumer, right, who doesn’t have any real need for this,” Luckey said.
But Luckey clearly hopes Anduril will eventually make U.S.-made laptops more in line with consumer desires. He said the product is the first in what he envisions as a full line of BlueChip computers, noting that he began his career making devices virtual reality headsets for consumers.
“I’m buying American cars, and then I buy a computer that’s made on the other side of the world, not just China, but you know, Japan, Korea,” he said. “It’s kind of humiliating that as an American and my birthright is computers, in my opinion, because America invented them, that I’m not able to buy an American computer.”
As for the potentially expensive folly of trying to take on China’s electronics components manufacturing industry single-handedly, Luckey joked about his internal reputation for “being a nut” with such big ideas. (He admits that he pushed his board to spend $900 million to build a factory for a jet before the company had even won a contract.)
“This is not one of those things. My investors do not think I’m a crazy person in this particular area,” he said. In fact, rugged computers are already about a $5 billion market .

articles.title_zh: Opera introduces a new web standard to let users deploy AI locally in their browser
articles.content_orig:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.
Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.
Browser maker Opera has introduced a new web standard that lets users to run AI models directly in its browser, without relying on the cloud.
The new standard, WebAI, is designed to work with a variety of AI models. Opera name drops Google’s Gemma — an open-weight model that Google first introduced two years ago — as one example. On Macs, WebAI also supports Apple’s on-device foundation model, the company says.
But Opera says WebAI isn’t tied to any particular model and is built to support a wide range of open-weight AI systems. WebAI grew out of previous work by Opera to bring locally run models into its browsers.
Opera is making the new AI features available as an early preview in its flagship Opera One browser. The company says Opera GX, its browser built for gamers and streamers, and Opera Neon, its browser that uses AI agents to perform tasks, will soon get the same treatment. Users have to choose to opt into the feature, according to the company.
Open-weight models offer a number of benefits to users. For one, they are typically free to download and use. Their underlying model weights are also publicly available, which gives developers more freedom to customize how they work. Although unlike fully open-source software, open-weight models still come with some restrictions.
There’s the additional advantage of privacy, the company said. Users can tap into AI features without having to send their personal information to a company’s servers or pay for a cloud-based AI subscription.
“Developers can add AI features without running AI infrastructure or paying for every request,” the company said in its announcement. “Users don’t need AI subscriptions, the information the local AI handles stays on their own device, and they stay in control of the AI on their computer.”
The company said WebAI also allows anyone to generate text, classify content, and understand how pieces of information relate, all directly in the browser.
Privacy has become a growing concern as AI assistants become more powerful and gain access to personal information. Users often surrender vast amounts of personal information with AI chatbots, sometimes without a clear understanding of how that data is stored or used.
Locally run models offer an alternative because the processing happens on the user’s own device — and not on a company’s cloud server. That doesn’t eliminate every privacy risk, but it does give users a bit more control. It makes sense then that Opera has made digital privacy one of its primary selling points over the years.
There are trade-offs, however. Running AI models locally puts more demand on a user’s computer, which can affect performance. Opera notes that model performance will depend on the  device’s hardware.

articles.title_orig: Why Netflix stock just can't catch a break after earnings
articles.title_zh: Why Netflix stock just can't catch a break after earnings
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
The dreadful year for Netflix ( NFLX ) investors just keeps getting more dreadful.
A fresh sell-off on the day after a lackluster earnings report on Oct. 20 has persisted, with Netflix shares down about 7% in the past five trading sessions. The S&P 500 is relatively flat during this stretch.
Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace analysis shows Netflix shares trading at one of the lowest trailing 12-month P/E ratios in the past decade.
Netflix stock is down 32% year to date.
If price is truth in the stock market, then Netflix's slide reflects its truths. They include lost viewership to rival YouTube, a less-than-hot content slate this year, and a view on Wall Street that content spending will have to increase dramatically in 2027 to regain eyeballs.
The third quarter for Netflix reflected all of this and then some.
Netflix delivered a mixed third quarter earnings report, with earnings of $0.87 per share, beating Wall Street estimates of $0.82. Revenue of $12.87 billion came in line with analysts' expectations.
For the fourth quarter, Netflix forecast revenue of $13.44 billion, below then expectations of $13.57 billion. The company also cut its full-year advertising revenue outlook to about $2.7 billion from $3 billion previously.
"The US is also working," Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos told analysts on an earnings call. "It's just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we'd like. We had some really solid doubles and triples this year. But the other territories count on some of those titles being home runs so that they'll travel around the world."
To reboot the bull case for the stock, Sarandos pushed the button on laying off 6% of the workforce. He sent well-regarded chief content officer Bela Bajaria packing in favor of former Disney ( DIS ) exec Peter Rice.
"2026 has been more of a transitional year than we envisioned. While the latest Ads miss is frustrating, we find comfort in Membership retention that is still healthy and corrective actions within content that can drive a potential re-acceleration in 2027E and into 2028E (which we are not modeling today)," KeyBanc analyst Justin Patterson said.

Apple's first foldable phone has just reached customers, and on October 26, 2026, the company admitted that some units are breaking at the fold.
Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) confirmed a defect in the inner folding display of the $1,999 iPhone Duo. The phone reached stores on October 23, after preorders sold out within minutes on October 16.
Shares fell 1.1%, or $3.81, to $343.91, then traded at $343.64 after hours. Part of that decline came from a bearish Jefferies note ahead of earnings and from a reaction to a pricier iPad mini, so the cracks add a new drag on pressure that was already there.
Apple is worth $5.019 trillion. That is roughly $19 billion above the $5 trillion mark it first closed above on October 14, 2026, at $342.96 a share.
A slide of about 0.4%, to near $342.60, would wipe out that buffer. Apple remains above that level, although routine headline risk is now likely enough to push it below.
Apple's statement read: "We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement."
Bloomberg confirmed the problem with more than half a dozen customers through photos and support records. Apple has not given a unit count, a cause, or a timeline for a fix.

iFixit gave the Duo a preliminary repairability score of 5 out of 10, its best for a foldable. The teardown also found a stress hotspot where the screen's curved fold presses down on the hinge's center support bar, near where breaks have been reported.

articles.title_orig: For Pope Leo, there was little choice but to go to Latin America
articles.title_zh: For Pope Leo, there was little choice but to go to Latin America
articles.content_orig:
"Brazil will not accept being anyone's backyard," Brazil's left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva declared in his election victory speech, a message squarely aimed at Washington.
Domestic elections are rarely won on foreign policy, and this one was no different. But Lula's defiance against what he has described as US interference in Brazilian affairs evoked a patriotic spirit that proved an effective campaigning tool.
It also chimed with his wider brand of politics as a former union leader: standing up to powerful figures.
Paradoxically, it seems to have earned him President Donald Trump's respect. "I like Lula, we get along well," Trump said, responding to the result. "I didn't take sides," he added, before calling the election "terrible" and "rigged".
Watch: How President Lula turned it around to beat FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro
If that sounds muddled, it is because the relationship between the two men is not straightforward. Trump did not explicitly endorse Lula's rival FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, who refused to recognise the result. But Trump was a close ally of FlÃ¡vio's father, the former President Jair Bolsonaro.
When I spoke to Lula at his residence about a year ago, relations had hit rock bottom. He told me he had "no relationship" with Trump, that they had never spoken, and that he had no intention of picking up the phone. Trump had recently imposed punitive tariffs on Brazil, largely as a political response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial, which the US president called a "witch-hunt" .
Rather than tiptoeing around Trump, as some US allies did, Lula fought back â and it paid off.
He made fiery speeches invoking Brazilian sovereignty, attacked US interference in the judicial process, and took to wearing a blue cap reading "Brazil belongs to Brazilians".
His approval ratings jumped.
He accused the Bolsonaro family, who had lobbied for the tariffs, of being unpatriotic â a blow to a political right that so often claims patriotism as its terrain.
Even some in the agricultural lobby, typically strong Bolsonaro supporters but reliant on US trade, thought Lula had a point.
The US eventually backed down and reduced the tariffs, although they have since risen again.
The two men spoke at the United Nations and later met in the Oval Office, where Trump called the talks "very good" and Lula said he left "very satisfied".
Another indication, perhaps, that Trump likes a strong leader.
Fireworks heard after Lula's victory in SÃ£o Paulo
So why might Trump be unhappy with the result?
Latin America has swung to the right, with Ecuador, Chile, Colombia, Argentina and Peru all electing presidents closely aligned with the Trump administration. Trump has sought to use these allies to establish US dominance in the Western Hemisphere, a strategy he has dubbed the "Donroe Doctrine".
Christopher Sabatini, senior fellow for Latin America at Chatham House, notes that Trump thought Brazil would be the "10th and biggest prize" after FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro won the first round.
Brazil is Latin America's largest economy, and the younger Bolsonaro was expected to join Trump's "Shield of Americas" coalition against narco-trafficking.
Brazil also holds the world's second-largest reserves of rare earth minerals after China, and the US had been eyeing preferential access.
The relationship has thawed, but with four more years ahead for Lula, several issues could reignite tensions.
Brazil accused the US earlier this year of trying to cast doubt on its electoral system and denied visas to two state department officials planning to visit.
The US called this "baseless" and revoked the Brazilian ambassador's visa in response.
If Trump keeps calling this result "rigged", further diplomatic fallout is likely.
Lula has also vehemently opposed US military action in the region, from the seizure of NicolÃ¡s Maduro in Venezuela to the bombing of alleged drug-trafficking vessels.
He lambasted Washington for designating Brazil's two major gangs as terrorist organisations after lobbying from FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, and warned of attacks on Brazilian sovereignty.
It is a sensitive subject for a political left that remembers the region's brutal 20th Century dictatorships, many backed by the CIA in the name of stopping communism.
Lula's campaign accused Meta of favouring FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro.
Meta denied this but admitted moderation issues and technical errors had wrongly removed some posts or limited their reach.
Lula's supporters responded by sharing his messages through a 10-million-strong WhatsApp group to bypass the algorithms.
Separately, the Trump administration is unhappy with Pix, Brazil's instant payment system, which has boosted the economy, but which the US sees as taking business from Visa and Mastercard.
The relationship has exposed political divisions.
In the campaign, Bolsonaro supporters waved US flags at their rallies and, in one case, an inflatable saying "Trump Nuke Brazil", while Lula and his supporters accused FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro of protecting US interests over Brazil's.
Still, tensions can be overstated.
The US remains Brazil's second-biggest trading partner after China, and for now the two leaders get on.
Whether that lasts will depend on how far the US tries to intervene in Brazilian affairs, and how bullish Lula is in response.

articles.title_orig: China’s economy may never overtake America — and it’s all due to an ill-fated 47-year-old policy
articles.title_zh: China’s economy may never overtake America — and it’s all due to an ill-fated 47-year-old policy
articles.content_orig:
Just one child doomed China’s hopes of overtaking the US.
The Middle Kingdom, once a surging economic growth engine expected to eclipse the US economy in just a few years, is not expected to outgrow the US until the 2040s now — if it does at all.
And it’s largely down to China’s 1979 One Child Policy , which is devastating growth, according to Yi Fuxian, a Chinese demographer at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Plummeting birth rates and economic problems have erased the 6+% per year growth that China reported before the COVID-19 pandemic.
Many economists in both China and the West were taken in by the Chinese Communist Party’s inflated official figures, which massively overestimated the country’s consumer power, Fuxian said.
It comes as a Goldman Sachs study found that China’s population began shrinking in 2022 , just 13 years after that of neighboring Japan. And its decline is on track to be far steeper, dramatically damaging the country’s economic prospects, the Financial Times reported .
China has a GDP of $21.6 trillion — just two-thirds the size of the US economy.
Yi told The Post that official Chinese statistics have systematically inflated the country’s birthrates and total population figures going back decades.
While official reports claim China has a population of over 1.4 billion, Yi calculates that the true figure in 2020 was “under 1.28 billion,” at least 130 million lower than reported.
India actually surpassed China as the world’s most populous nation years earlier than officially recognized, according to Yi, author of the 2007 book, “Big Country with an Empty Nest,” which criticized China’s one-child policies.
The US, the third most populous country in the world, has 342 million people — about a quarter the population of China.
Yi argues that China’s population actually began shrinking in 2018, four years earlier than Goldman Sachs’ estimate, and more than a decade before the official projection of 2031 to 2034.
Most of this can be attributed to China’s notorious One Child Policy , instituted to limit Chinese families to one child per mother, over fears of spiraling population growth and widespread poverty.
While the policy was relaxed to two children per couple in 2016 and three children in 2021, China’s total fertility rate remains one of the lowest in the world .
China is no longer poor — officially 0% of the population is in extreme poverty, compared to 88% 40 years ago.
But it’s also not rich; the per capita GDP is about $13,800 per year, about 15% of that in the US.
Turkey, Russia and Kazakhstan are all richer than China by that measure.
The country’s total fertility rate fell below the 2.1 replacement level in 1991 and continued to plummet, dropping below 1.0 and now estimated to be just 0.8 births per woman, according to Yi.
Last year saw a record low of just 8 million live births in China. The much smaller US, by contrast, had 3.6 million births.
Yi also blames the economic reforms of China’s former Premier Zhu Rongji in the 1990s, for causing “many problems” that slowed down China’s economic growth and race to catch up with the US.
Decades of strict birth restrictions and fiscal centralization severely curtailed household disposable income in China, to roughly 42-44% of GDP.
In contrast, in the US, that figure is over 70% of GDP.
While this may have helped China’s economy in the short term, allowing it to flood the US with cheap imported goods, in the long run, it may have signed the CCP’s suicide note, according to Yi.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
Children function as “super-consumers,” driving much of household spending, he explained.
With China missing several full generations worth of children, this severely crippled Chinese domestic consumption, he argued.
To offset weak domestic consumption, China became heavily dependent on manufacturing exports, an unsustainable real estate bubble, and state-subsidized industrial overcapacity, he explained.
Those policies, “killed China’s economy, the population and the economy — and also killed America’s manufacturing,” Yi said.
China is now one of the oldest countries in the world, with a rapidly shrinking labor pool and aging population. The median age is expected to reach 59 by 2050, compared to 44 in the US.
This means Beijing may never catch up with the US economically — and worse, could face a long-term economic deceleration, Yi argued.
Yi puts the over-optimistic predictions about China’s economic growth down to mainstream economists and Chinese government-aligned institutions relying on fabricated data — assuming China’s population would soon grow five times larger than the US.
This played into the popular narrative that “the East is rising while the West is declining,” he said, while the truth is very different.
“By 2029 to 2035, China will lag behind the US across all major demographic and growth metrics,” Yi said.
However, for pro-democracy activists who might hope that this demographic time bomb could topple the CCP, Yi has a warning.
Contrary to Western expectations that economic development would foster a pro-democracy middle class, China’s rapid aging has depleted it of the young population required to drive political activism.
Just 16% of China is aged 15 to 29, down from 31% at the time of China’s last mass-democracy movement in 1989, which culminated in the communists’ brutal crackdown in Tiananmen Square.
An aging, risk-averse China is far more likely to support a centralized strongman who will safeguard pensions and social stability, Yi explained.

articles.title_orig: Boeing narrows third-quarter loss as defense sales rise, but focus remains on 737 Max production
articles.title_zh: Boeing narrows third-quarter loss as defense sales rise, but focus remains on 737 Max production
articles.content_orig:
Boeing doesn't expect to significantly ramp up output of its best-selling 737 Max aircraft until the second half of 2027 as it grapples with a slower-than-expected pace of wing production.
CEO Kelly Ortberg said Tuesday on the company's quarterly earnings call that Boeing is targeting a production rate of 52 planes a month in the second half of 2027. It has been manufacturing about 47 of its 737 Max planes a month.
Ortberg had told investors last month that the production stabilize was taking a "little bit longer" than expected becuase of the wings production pace.
Boeing stock was down about 9% during the call.
"I know everybody wants us to go faster but we're going to do it right," Ortberg told CNBC's Phil LeBeau in an interview Tuesday.
Ortberg reiterated the company's priority in stabilizing production on Tuesday.
"Looking ahead, expectations are rising, and they should," Ortberg said in a note to staff on Tuesday. "That means elevating our performance through lean, productivity and efficiency improvements in our day-to-day work while upholding our high levels of safety and quality."
Aircraft production and deliveries are key to Boeing's recovery since the bulk of an aircraft's price is paid when the customer receives it.
The company also reported Tuesday that it narrowed its losses in the third quarter, thanks to a boost from its defense unit.
For the three months ended Sept. 30, Boeing reported a net loss of $116 million, or 26 cents a share, compared with a $5.34 billion loss, or $7.14 per share, a year earlier. Adjusting for one-time items, the company posted a loss of 34 cents a share. A year earlier, Boeing had taken a nearly $5 billion charge on its long-delayed 777X aircraft program.
Revenue climbed 4% on the year to $24.19 billion. Free cash flow rose to $464 million from $238 million in the third quarter of 2025.
The company's defense unit revenue jumped 15% in the third quarter from a year earlier to $7.94 billion.
Here's what Boeing reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street analysts expected, according to consensus estimates from LSEG:
Boeing delivered 161 commercial airplanes in the third quarter, one more jet than a year earlier.
Revenue in the all-important commercial aircraft business fell 3% to $10.72 billion. The unit had a negative operating margin of 6.5% because of a "less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs," Boeing said.
Ortberg told staff in a memo that the manufacturer has "more work to do."
The manufacturer had some wins lately. The U.S. Navy tapped Boeing to develop its next-generation fighter jet.
And the Federal Aviation Administration last week signed off on the 737 Max 10 , the largest in the Max family. That followed the approval of the 737 Max 7 in August and marked the final certifications for the aircraft line.

Two men face national security charges after a suspected Iran-linked incident at RAF Fairford, a key U.S. bomber base in the United Kingdom.
British prosecutors charged two men Tuesday under the U.K.’s National Security Act following an incident at RAF Fairford, a key base used by the U.S. military’s heavy bombers.
Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, of London, was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service. Nouman Essghir, 24, was charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the United Kingdom, according to the Crown Prosecution Service.
British counterterrorism police said they believe the foreign country Abdulkarim was assisting was Iran, Reuters reported.

(Photo by Matthew Horwood/Getty Images)
The charges follow a September incident near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, England. British police arrested five men outside the base in the early hours of Sept. 27, according to Reuters.
The base had been used by U.S. bombers to carry out strikes against Iran . About a dozen B-1 bombers were among the aircraft later withdrawn from RAF Fairford and returned to their home stations in the United States on security grounds, according to previous Fox News reporting.

Several men have been arrested on suspicion of offences under the explosives act, and the Army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are examining a number of vehicles in the area. RAF Fairford serves as a key European operating location for U.S. heavy bombers and has supported American military missions.
Frank Ferguson, chief crown prosecutor for the CPS Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division, said the agency decided to prosecute the two men following a "complex" counterterrorism investigation .

"We will continue to work closely with our partners as this complex investigation continues," Ferguson said.
Both men were expected to appear Tuesday at Westminster Magistrates’ Court.

articles.title_orig: Climber falls nearly 5,000 feet to his death on Nepal mountain after reaching summit
articles.title_zh: Climber falls nearly 5,000 feet to his death on Nepal mountain after reaching summit
articles.content_orig:
A German climber fell about 1,500 meters (nearly 5,000 feet) to his death on Monday, a day after reaching the summit of Ama Dablam mountain, according to a trekking company operator.
Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, was reported missing from Camp 3, which lies at around 6,200 meters. He had been resting after reaching the 6,812-meter summit on Sunday, before his planned descent.
"After a successful summit, he spent a night at Camp 3 on Sunday, and on Monday morning, his guide found him missing," Gokul Thapa, head of the trekking company Real Himalaya, told AFP.
Thapa said Waschiczek's personal trekking guide, Sonam Lama, had left him in the tent for a few minutes to return borrowed equipment, telling him to stay inside. When he returned, Waschiczek was missing.
Waschiczek's body was spotted by another Sherpa at Camp 2 at around 8 am on Monday at an altitude of about 4,600 metres, Thapa said.
The body was retrieved by helicopter during the afternoon and taken to Lukla, a town known as a gateway for mountaineers and trekkers heading to the Everest region.
It was then flown to the capital, Kathmandu, where a postmortem will be performed at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.
"Once the postmortem is done, the body will be handed over to his family members through the embassy," Thapa told AFP.
He said this was Waschiczek's second visit to Nepal.
"He had come to Nepal in 2024 for a trek, and his passing saddened us," he added.
Two Japanese climbers died last week on another peak in west Nepal, the Reuters news agency reported .
Ama Dablam lies in Nepal's Khumbu region and is considered a technically challenging mountain with steep faces.
This is the first fatality on the mountain this year.
Last October, two climbers, one French, aged 65, and the other South Korean, aged 66, died during expeditions there.
This climbing season, more than 300 climbers are attempting to scale Ama Dablam.
Mountaineers have died on other peaks this year.
In July, famed British Nepali climber Nirmal Purja and nine other climbers were killed after being swept away by an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak.
In May, two Indian climbers died on Mount Everest during a record-breaking period of ascents via Nepal's southern route.
In May, American climber Shelley Johannesen died in an avalanche on Nepal's Mount Makalu. Johannesen, co-founder of U.S.-based outfitter Dash Adventures, had successfully reached the 27,838-foot summit before she was struck by an avalanche at around 23,600 feet while coming down.

articles.title_orig: iPhone 18e Could Get Two Key Upgrades While Keeping 60Hz Display
articles.title_zh: iPhone 18e Could Get Two Key Upgrades While Keeping 60Hz Display
articles.content_orig:
Apple's upcoming iPhone 18e model will retain a 60Hz display but could gain an upgraded front-facing camera, according to the leaker known as "Digital Chat Station."
In a new post on Weibo, the leaker said that the device will feature a 6.12-inch OLED display using low-temperature polycrystalline silicon (LTPS) technology, the A20 chip, and a single 48-megapixel rear camera. They were less definitive about the front-facing camera, saying it could be upgraded to 24 megapixels.
The specifications suggest that the iPhone 18e will offer no major display or rear camera hardware upgrades over the previous two generations. Both the iPhone 16e and iPhone 17e feature approximately 6.1-inch ‌OLED‌ displays with a 60Hz refresh rate and a single 48-megapixel rear camera. The post does not detail the rear camera's sensor or lens, so smaller hardware changes remain possible.
The A20 chip would represent a more significant upgrade. Like the A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro , the A20 is expected to use a 2nm manufacturing process , bringing notable performance and power efficiency improvements over the iPhone 17e 's 3nm A19 chip. It would also bring the device into line with the upcoming standard iPhone 18 , which is expected to use the same chip .
The front-facing camera claim is less clear. Digital Chat Station specified 24 megapixels, although it is unclear whether this refers to a new camera or is a mistaken reference to the 18-megapixel Center Stage camera introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup. A 24-megapixel camera was widely rumored before those devices launched. Either resolution would represent an upgrade over the 12-megapixel front camera used by the iPhone 16e and ‌iPhone 17e‌.
Digital Chat Station previously claimed that the iPhone 18e would retain a 60Hz LTPS display. An earlier report from Korea suggested that an LTPO display capable of supporting 120Hz ProMotion could reach the entry-level iPhone with the "iPhone 19e" in 2028.
The iPhone 18e is expected to launch in spring 2027 , alongside the standard ‌iPhone 18‌ and iPhone Air 2.

articles.title_orig: China’s fifth plenum focuses on discipline and loyalty to Xi
articles.title_zh: China’s fifth plenum focuses on discipline and loyalty to Xi
articles.content_orig:
Plenums are essentially closed door meetings of the Party's central committee that happen at least once a year
A major political gathering is under way in the Chinese capital, with a closed-door meeting of senior figures that could shape the look of the ruling Communist Party in the years to come.
The Fifth Plenum brings together around 300 members of the Central Committee and state media said it would pave the way for a "tightening of discipline" within the Party's ranks.
The four-day session that started on Monday will give Xi Jinping an opportunity to further consolidate his grip on power following recent purges.
The normally annual plenums are highly secretive, but a summary of decisions and a more detailed document will be made public after.
They are essentially closed door meetings of the Party's central committee that happen at least once a year.
There are usually seven plenums during each five-year Central Committee term and they are watched from afar because they are meant to signal the leadership's priorities.
The timing for this year's gathering is important because it is a year away from the next Party Congress, where a new set of priorities is set up and a new central committee appointed.
Officially, the Central Committee selects the Party's top leadership but the real processes leading to the selection are kept secret within the Party elite.
The next Party Congress will almost certainly reappoint Xi as the country's leader, following the abolition of term limits.
Past plenum sessions have been used to declare Xi as "the core" of the Party, abolish term limits which cleared the way for him to remain in power indefinitely, and elevate his personal philosophy â branded as "Xi Jinping Thought" â to the same level as Chairman Mao.
This year's plenum is an opportunity for Xi to dictate strategy in the run up to the Congress, ensuring that views are aligned and delegates loyal.
Even the location of the meeting, which will wrap up on Thursday, has not been announced. Past plenums have been held inside Beijing's Jingxi Hotel.
According to a readout from the powerful 21-member Politburo this September,  the plenum will adopt a decision on "several major issues persistently advancing the comprehensive strict governance of the Party", which is being read as a way to further ensure obedience and effectiveness from distant party officials.
This means it would also be a time of nervousness for delegates as they look around the room with its "empty chairs" following the scale of recent purges within the Party.
Allegations of corruption, even "moral corruption", have seen large swathes of senior figures culled.
"Moral corruption" has been seen by experts as a way of cracking down on perceived disloyalty to Xi because overall disloyalty to the Party can be interpreted as a breach of "morality".
The Asia Society Policy Institute has estimated that of 44 military members appointed to the Central Committee in 2022 only two have not been taken down.
The all-powerful seven-man Central Military Commission, which runs the armed forces in China, has also been whittled down to only two people, Xi Jinping and one other general.
This plenum is an opportunity for him to appoint new officers to this body.

articles.title_orig: GM will switch to Nasdaq from the NYSE on Nov. 17
articles.title_zh: GM will switch to Nasdaq from the NYSE on Nov. 17
articles.content_orig:
DETROIT — General Motors plans to transfer shares of its common stock from the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq as the automaker attempts to position itself more as a technology-focused company.
The Detroit automaker said Tuesday that it expects to begin trading as a Nasdaq -listed company on Nov. 17. Its ticker symbol is expected to remain "GM," the company said.
"GM's customer-focused, technology-driven strategy is creating value for our stockholders, making Nasdaq a natural home for our listing as we grow," GM CFO Paul Jacobson said in a release. "We're grateful for our long-standing partnership with the New York Stock Exchange and its remarkable legacy."
GM noted the move will provide eligibility for potential inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index .
Current shareholders do not need to take any action with respect to the transfer, the company said.
The switch marks a notable loss for the NYSE, as GM first listed on the exchange in 1911. The Detroit automaker also relisted on the stock exchange in 2010 following a government-backed bankruptcy.
GM follows other companies such as Walmart , DoorDash and Palantir Technologies that have transferred from the more traditional NYSE to the historically technology focused Nasdaq in recent years. Hilton Worldwide Holdings last week also announced plans to move trading from the NYSE to Nasdaq.
The key drivers for a listing transfer differ from company to company, but the Nasdaq in 2024 said common reasons include "index inclusion opportunities, cost effective fee structure, brand visibility partnership, access to Nasdaq's event space, and Nasdaq's suite of investor relations and ESG products."
GM's decision comes a week after the automaker held a technology-focused event where executives laid out the company's roadmap for artificial intelligence and self-driving vehicle technologies.
Shares of GM, which has been aggressively buying back stock , have more than doubled since 2024. GM's stock closed Monday at $76.31 per share. The company's market cap is roughly $64.4 billion.

articles.title_orig: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices : Planet Money
articles.title_zh: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices : Planet Money
articles.content_orig:
Aldi is expanding its footprint in the United States by offering lower grocery prices through private-label products, a limited assortment of goods and cost-conscious store operations. The German discount retailer has gained ground as food costs have increased since the pandemic, putting pressure on household budgets and intensifying competition among grocery chains. According to Bloomberg, Aldi plans to operate more than 3,000 US locations by the end of 2028, potentially making it the country's second-largest grocery chain by store count after Walmart.
The company generated approximately $29 billion in US sales in 2024, exceeding Trader Joe's sales, according to the source article. Food reporter Deena Shanker found through months of price comparisons that Aldi's prices generally matched Walmart's or came in slightly lower. Other retailers, including Wegmans and Kroger, have announced price reductions in response to competitive pressure.
An analysis published in late 2023 found that grocery chains reduced their markups by approximately 7% in areas where Lidl, another German discount grocer with a similar business model, opened stores.
Aldi's strategy relies heavily on products sold under its own brands. Instead of stocking predominantly national brands, the retailer sells alternatives such as Benton's Chocolate Sandwich Cookies with Vanilla Filling and Savoritz Golden Round crackers. Because Aldi controls these private-label products, it avoids paying the markup associated with purchasing established national brands before adding its own retail margin. More than 80% of the products on Aldi's shelves are store-brand items, according to the source article.
The company's limited product selection also reduces costs. When brothers Albrecht took over their family's grocery store in 1946, restricted funds and limited space encouraged them to concentrate on essential goods rather than offer numerous brands, sizes and varieties. That approach allows Aldi to purchase larger quantities of selected products while reducing the need for extensive storage and shelf space. Carrying fewer niche items also limits the risk of spoilage and lowers real estate and operating expenses.
Aldi applies similar cost-conscious principles to its store operations. Employees place products on shelves in the cardboard shipping boxes rather than unpacking and arranging every item individually, reducing labor requirements. Stores also forgo background music, avoiding associated equipment and licensing costs.
However, shoppers may need to visit another retailer to find products Aldi does not carry, including less common ingredients. The restricted assortment is a trade-off for the lower prices available on stocked items. Cost control alone does not explain the retailer's continued appeal.
Aldi has also developed a reputation for rotating special purchases, including toys, German spätzle and seasonal advent calendars containing 24 cheeses.
The chain has broadened its offerings to attract a wider range of customers, including higher-income shoppers. Its selection includes premium products and Honeycrisp apples, allowing the retailer to compete on price across more than just basic grocery staples.
Economic conditions have also supported Aldi's expansion. The Great Recession helped strengthen the retailer's position as consumers sought cheaper food, while the more recent rise in food prices has renewed interest in discount grocery shopping. Aldi's growth comes as American households face a shift from the long-term trend of spending a smaller share of income on food. From 1960 to 2019, Americans generally devoted a declining proportion of their income to food, but food became less affordable after the pandemic, according to the source article.

articles.title_orig: Man charged with assisting ‘foreign intelligence service’ after incident at UK base used for Iran strikes
articles.title_zh: Man charged with assisting ‘foreign intelligence service’ after incident at UK base used for Iran strikes
articles.content_orig:
The U.K. has said it had charged a man with an offense of assisting a "foreign intelligence service" over an incident at a military base used by the U.S. for strikes on Iran.
Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, has been charged under the country's National Security Act "following an incident involving RAF Fairford," an air base in west England, prosecutors announced on Tuesday .
Between Aug. 31 and Sept. 28, Abdulkarim is alleged to have engaged in "conduct that would likely materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out U.K.-related activities", the Crown Prosecution Service added. The foreign country was not named.
Prosecutors also charged 24-year-old Nouman Essghir with "entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK".
The men are due to appear in court in London on Tuesday.
Five people were arrested on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offenses near RAF Fairford on Sept. 28. The base had been used as the U.S. Air Force's command outpost for operations from Europe and for American strikes on Iranian missile sites.
Announcing the charges, Frank Ferguson, a chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service's Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division, said that they followed "a Counter Terrorism Policing investigation into a high-profile incident involving RAF Fairford."
"We will continue to work closely with our partners as this complex investigation continues," he said.
After the arrests, U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. had moved its long-range bombers out of the U.K. in response to a threat "linked to Iran."
Prime Minister Andy Burnham told lawmakers earlier this month that the incident was "highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard."
Over the summer, Iran's Revolutionary Guard warned it saw any military base involved in launching airstrikes on Iran as a legitimate target.
Tehran denied any involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford.

articles.title_orig: Two British Men Charged Over Major Security Incident at U.K. Air Base
articles.title_zh: Two British Men Charged Over Major Security Incident at U.K. Air Base
articles.content_orig:
Oct. 27 (UPI) -- Authorities in Britain on Tuesday charged a 24-year-old man with spying for a foreign intelligence service, allegedly Iran, in relation to an incident at RAF Fairford in September in which a group of masked men in vans were arrested by counter-terrorism police near the base in the middle of the night.
The Crown Prosecution Service said in a news release that Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim of London was charged under the National Security Act with assisting a foreign intelligence service by carrying out activities in Britain between Aug. 31 and Sept. 28 "likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service."
"In this case, we believe that country to be Iran ," said Head of National Counter Terrorism Policing, Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor.
A second man, Nouman Essghir, 24 and also from London, was charged with a single National Security offense that on Aug. 22 he entered, scoped out or got too close to a prohibited place "for a purpose prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom."
Both men are due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court later on Tuesday.
Five others arrested on suspicion of explosives offenses during the alleged Sept. 27 incident in the Gloucestershire village of Whelford, a half mile from the base, and then re-arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act, are free on police bail, Counter Terrorism Policing said.
CTP added that an eighth man, a 25-year-old dual British-Iranian national who was re-arrested last week, has been released without charge but remains on strict police bail.
"We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state, and as the Director General of MI5 said just the other week, we are working together to intervene, identify and respond to that threat," said CTP Assistant Commissioner Taylor.
RAF Fairford had been used by the U.S. military to fly missions amid its war with Iran.
A week after the security incident, the United States pulled out all of its bomber aircraft -- at least a dozen long-range B-1s -- stationed at the base, citing "threats."
